entries.name: MassUnit.div_mul_div
entries.docstring: The unit-ratio cocycle at `ℝ≥0` (the un-coerced form of `div_mul_div_coe`).
entries.snippet: lemma div_mul_div (x y z : MassUnit) : (x / y) * (y / z) = x / z

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum
entries.docstring:
The simple gravity pendulum is specified by the mass `m` of its bob, the length `ℓ` of its
  rod, and the gravitational acceleration `g`. All three are assumed to be positive. The
  configuration of the pendulum is the angle of the rod from the downward vertical.
entries.snippet:
structure SimplePendulum where
  m : ℝ
  ℓ : ℝ
  g : ℝ
  m_pos : 0 < m
  ℓ_pos : 0 < ℓ
  g_pos : 0 < g

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.m_ne_zero
entries.docstring: The mass of the bob is not equal to zero.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma m_ne_zero : S.m ≠ 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ℓ_ne_zero
entries.docstring: The length of the rod is not equal to zero.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ℓ_ne_zero : S.ℓ ≠ 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.g_ne_zero
entries.docstring: The gravitational acceleration is not equal to zero.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma g_ne_zero : S.g ≠ 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ω
entries.docstring:
The angular frequency of the simple pendulum, `ω`, is defined as `√(g/ℓ)`. It is the angular
  frequency of the small oscillations of the pendulum about the bottom of its swing.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def ω : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ω_pos
entries.docstring: The angular frequency of the simple pendulum is positive.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ω_pos : 0 < S.ω

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ω_ne_zero
entries.docstring: The angular frequency of the simple pendulum is not equal to zero.
entries.snippet: lemma ω_ne_zero : S.ω ≠ 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ω_sq
entries.docstring: The square of the angular frequency of the simple pendulum is equal to `g/ℓ`.
entries.snippet: lemma ω_sq : S.ω ^ 2 = S.g / S.ℓ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.inverse_ω_sq
entries.docstring: The inverse of the square of the angular frequency of the simple pendulum is `ℓ/g`.
entries.snippet: lemma inverse_ω_sq : (S.ω ^ 2)⁻¹ = S.ℓ / S.g

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.inertia
entries.docstring:
The moment of inertia of the simple pendulum about its pivot is `I = m ℓ²`, the moment of
  inertia of a point mass `m` at distance `ℓ` from the axis.
entries.snippet: def inertia : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.inertia_pos
entries.docstring: The moment of inertia of the simple pendulum is positive.
entries.snippet: lemma inertia_pos : 0 < S.inertia

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.inertia_ne_zero
entries.docstring: The moment of inertia of the simple pendulum is not equal to zero.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma inertia_ne_zero : S.inertia ≠ 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ω_sq_mul_inertia
entries.docstring:
The square of the angular frequency times the moment of inertia is `m g ℓ`, the coefficient
  appearing in the potential energy and in the torque. This is the identity by which the mass
  cancels from the equation of motion.
entries.snippet: lemma ω_sq_mul_inertia : S.ω ^ 2 * S.inertia = S.m * S.g * S.ℓ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.kineticEnergy
entries.docstring:
The kinetic energy of the simple pendulum along a lift `θ` of the angle is
  $\frac{1}{2} I ‖\dot θ‖^2$, where `I` is the moment of inertia about the pivot.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def kineticEnergy (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) : Time → ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.potentialEnergy
entries.docstring:
The potential energy of the simple pendulum at the angle `x` is `m g ℓ (1 - cos (x 0))`, the
  work done against gravity in raising the bob from the bottom of the swing. It is normalized to
  vanish at the bottom.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def potentialEnergy (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.energy
entries.docstring: The energy of the simple pendulum is the kinetic energy plus the potential energy.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def energy (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) : Time → ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.kineticEnergy_eq
entries.docstring: The kinetic energy of the simple pendulum, written out.
entries.snippet:
lemma kineticEnergy_eq (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.kineticEnergy θ = fun t => (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * S.inertia * ⟪∂ₜ θ t, ∂ₜ θ t⟫_ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.potentialEnergy_eq
entries.docstring: The potential energy of the simple pendulum, written out.
entries.snippet:
lemma potentialEnergy_eq (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.potentialEnergy x = S.m * S.g * S.ℓ * (1 - Real.cos (x 0))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.energy_eq
entries.docstring: The energy of the simple pendulum, written out.
entries.snippet:
lemma energy_eq (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.energy θ = fun t => S.kineticEnergy θ t + S.potentialEnergy (θ t)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.potentialEnergy_nonneg
entries.docstring:
The potential energy of the simple pendulum is non-negative, the bottom of the swing being
  the lowest point of the circle on which the bob moves.
entries.snippet: lemma potentialEnergy_nonneg (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) : 0 ≤ S.potentialEnergy x

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.potentialEnergy_le
entries.docstring:
The potential energy of the simple pendulum is at most `2 m g ℓ`, its value at the top of the
  swing.
entries.snippet:
lemma potentialEnergy_le (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.potentialEnergy x ≤ 2 * (S.m * S.g * S.ℓ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.potentialEnergy_eq_zero_iff
entries.docstring:
The potential energy of the simple pendulum vanishes exactly when the cosine of the angle is
  equal to `1`, that is exactly at the bottom of the swing.
entries.snippet:
lemma potentialEnergy_eq_zero_iff (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.potentialEnergy x = 0 ↔ Real.cos (x 0) = 1

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.potentialEnergy_contDiff
entries.docstring: The potential energy of the simple pendulum is a smooth function of the angle.
entries.snippet:
@[fun_prop]
lemma potentialEnergy_contDiff (n : WithTop ℕ∞) : ContDiff ℝ n S.potentialEnergy

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.differentiable_potentialEnergy
entries.docstring:
The potential energy of the simple pendulum is a differentiable function of the angle. This
  is differentiability in the angle; for differentiability in time along a smooth lift of the
  angle see `potentialEnergy_differentiable`.
entries.snippet:
@[fun_prop]
lemma differentiable_potentialEnergy : Differentiable ℝ S.potentialEnergy

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.gradient_potentialEnergy
entries.docstring:
The gradient of the potential energy of the simple pendulum is `m g ℓ sin θ` times the unit
  vector of the angular coordinate.
entries.snippet:
lemma gradient_potentialEnergy (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    gradient S.potentialEnergy x =
      (S.m * S.g * S.ℓ * Real.sin (x 0)) • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.kineticEnergy_differentiable
entries.docstring: Along a smooth lift of the angle the kinetic energy is differentiable in time.
entries.snippet:
@[fun_prop]
lemma kineticEnergy_differentiable (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) :
    Differentiable ℝ (S.kineticEnergy θ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.potentialEnergy_differentiable
entries.docstring:
Along a smooth lift of the angle the potential energy is a differentiable function of the
  time. This is differentiability in time along the lift; for differentiability in the angle see
  `differentiable_potentialEnergy`.
entries.snippet:
@[fun_prop]
lemma potentialEnergy_differentiable (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun t => S.potentialEnergy (θ t))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.energy_differentiable
entries.docstring: Along a smooth lift of the angle the energy is differentiable in time.
entries.snippet:
@[fun_prop]
lemma energy_differentiable (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) :
    Differentiable ℝ (S.energy θ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.kineticEnergy_deriv
entries.docstring:
The rate of change of the kinetic energy is the angular velocity paired with the angular
  momentum's rate of change, `I θ̈`.
entries.snippet:
lemma kineticEnergy_deriv (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) :
    ∂ₜ (S.kineticEnergy θ) = fun t => ⟪∂ₜ θ t, S.inertia • ∂ₜ (∂ₜ θ) t⟫_ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.potentialEnergy_deriv
entries.docstring:
The rate of change of the potential energy is the angular velocity paired with the gradient
  of the potential.
entries.snippet:
lemma potentialEnergy_deriv (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) :
    ∂ₜ (fun t => S.potentialEnergy (θ t)) =
      fun t => ⟪∂ₜ θ t, gradient S.potentialEnergy (θ t)⟫_ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.energy_deriv
entries.docstring:
The rate of change of the energy is the angular velocity paired with the sum of `I θ̈` and
  the gradient of the potential; the equation of motion is exactly the vanishing of that sum.
entries.snippet:
lemma energy_deriv (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) :
    ∂ₜ (S.energy θ) =
      fun t => ⟪∂ₜ θ t, S.inertia • ∂ₜ (∂ₜ θ) t + gradient S.potentialEnergy (θ t)⟫_ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.lagrangian
entries.docstring:
The Lagrangian of the simple pendulum, `L(t, θ, θ̇) = ½ I ‖θ̇‖² - V(θ)`, the kinetic energy
  minus the potential energy as a function on phase space. It does not depend on the time.
entries.snippet:
@[nolint unusedArguments]
noncomputable def lagrangian (t : Time) (x v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.lagrangian_eq
entries.docstring: The Lagrangian of the simple pendulum, written out in the input data.
entries.snippet:
lemma lagrangian_eq :
    S.lagrangian = fun _ x v =>
      (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * S.inertia * ⟪v, v⟫_ℝ - S.m * S.g * S.ℓ * (1 - Real.cos (x 0))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.lagrangian_eq_kineticEnergy_sub_potentialEnergy
entries.docstring:
Along a lift of the angle the Lagrangian of the simple pendulum is the kinetic energy minus
  the potential energy.
entries.snippet:
lemma lagrangian_eq_kineticEnergy_sub_potentialEnergy (t : Time)
    (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.lagrangian t (θ t) (∂ₜ θ t) = S.kineticEnergy θ t - S.potentialEnergy (θ t)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.contDiff_lagrangian
entries.docstring:
The Lagrangian of the simple pendulum is a smooth function of the time, the angle and the
  angular velocity jointly.
entries.snippet:
@[fun_prop]
lemma contDiff_lagrangian (n : WithTop ℕ∞) : ContDiff ℝ n ↿S.lagrangian

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.gradient_lagrangian_position_eq
entries.docstring:
The gradient of the Lagrangian of the simple pendulum in the angle is minus the gradient of
  the potential energy, `-m g ℓ sin θ` times the unit vector of the angular coordinate.
entries.snippet:
lemma gradient_lagrangian_position_eq (t : Time) (x v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    gradient (fun x => S.lagrangian t x v) x =
      -((S.m * S.g * S.ℓ * Real.sin (x 0)) • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.gradient_lagrangian_velocity_eq
entries.docstring:
The gradient of the Lagrangian of the simple pendulum in the angular velocity is the angular
  momentum `I θ̇` about the pivot.
entries.snippet:
lemma gradient_lagrangian_velocity_eq (t : Time) (x v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    gradient (S.lagrangian t x) v = S.inertia • v

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.torque
entries.docstring:
The generalized force of the simple pendulum conjugate to the angle, that is the torque about
  the pivot, is minus the gradient of the potential energy, `τ = -∂V/∂θ`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def torque (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.torque_eq
entries.docstring:
The torque of the simple pendulum is `-m g ℓ sin θ` times the unit vector of the angular
  coordinate. It is restoring near the bottom of the swing: for `|θ| < π` it opposes the
  displacement, and it vanishes both at the bottom and at the inverted position.
entries.snippet:
lemma torque_eq (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.torque x = -((S.m * S.g * S.ℓ * Real.sin (x 0)) • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.torque_apply
entries.docstring: The single component of the torque of the simple pendulum is `-m g ℓ sin θ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma torque_apply (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.torque x 0 = -(S.m * S.g * S.ℓ * Real.sin (x 0))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.EquationOfMotion
entries.docstring:
The equation of motion of the simple pendulum: at every instant the rate of change `I θ̈` of
  the angular momentum about the pivot equals the torque `τ(θ)` of gravity.

  This pointwise relation, and not the vanishing of the variational derivative of the action, is
  the definition of the equation of motion here; see the discussion in section E. For a smooth
  lift of the angle the two agree, by `equationOfMotion_iff_gradLagrangian_zero` of section G.
entries.snippet: def EquationOfMotion (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) : Prop

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.equationOfMotion_iff_newtons_2nd_law
entries.docstring:
The equation of motion of the simple pendulum with all of its terms on one side: at every
  instant the rate of change `I θ̈` of the angular momentum plus the gradient of the potential
  energy vanishes. This is the rotational form of Newton's second law, in the shape in which
  `DampedHarmonicOscillator` states its own; the sum on the left is exactly the combination that
  `energy_deriv` pairs with the velocity `∂ₜ θ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma equationOfMotion_iff_newtons_2nd_law (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.EquationOfMotion θ ↔
      ∀ t, S.inertia • ∂ₜ (∂ₜ θ) t + gradient S.potentialEnergy (θ t) = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.IsSolution
entries.docstring:
A solution of the simple pendulum is a smooth lift of the angle satisfying the equation of
  motion.
entries.snippet: def IsSolution (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) : Prop

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.IsSolution.contDiff
entries.docstring: A solution of the simple pendulum is smooth.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsSolution.contDiff {S : SimplePendulum} {θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)}
    (h : S.IsSolution θ) : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.IsSolution.equationOfMotion
entries.docstring: A solution of the simple pendulum satisfies the equation of motion.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsSolution.equationOfMotion {S : SimplePendulum} {θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)}
    (h : S.IsSolution θ) : S.EquationOfMotion θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.equationOfMotion_iff_scalar
entries.docstring:
The equation of motion of the simple pendulum in scalar form, `θ̈ + ω² sin θ = 0`. The mass
  has cancelled: only the angular frequency `ω = √(g/ℓ)` survives.
entries.snippet:
lemma equationOfMotion_iff_scalar (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.EquationOfMotion θ ↔ ∀ t, ∂ₜ (∂ₜ θ) t 0 + S.ω ^ 2 * Real.sin (θ t 0) = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.equationOfMotion_iff_of_eq_ω
entries.docstring:
Two simple pendulums with the same angular frequency have the same angular equation of
  motion, and hence the same angular motions; in particular, changing only the mass does not
  affect the angular motion. An equal `ω` still permits different lengths, and so different
  trajectories of the bob in space.
entries.snippet:
lemma equationOfMotion_iff_of_eq_ω (S' : SimplePendulum) (h : S'.ω = S.ω)
    (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S'.EquationOfMotion θ ↔ S.EquationOfMotion θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.gradLagrangian
entries.docstring:
The variational derivative of the action of the simple pendulum, the action being the time
  integral of the Lagrangian along a lift of the angle.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def gradLagrangian (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.gradLagrangian_eq_eulerLagrangeOp
entries.docstring:
For a smooth lift of the angle the variational derivative of the action of the simple
  pendulum is the Euler–Lagrange operator of its Lagrangian.
entries.snippet:
lemma gradLagrangian_eq_eulerLagrangeOp (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) :
    S.gradLagrangian θ = eulerLagrangeOp S.lagrangian θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.gradLagrangian_eq_torque
entries.docstring:
For a smooth lift of the angle the variational derivative of the action of the simple
  pendulum is the torque minus the rate of change `I θ̈` of the angular momentum.
entries.snippet:
lemma gradLagrangian_eq_torque (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) :
    S.gradLagrangian θ = fun t => S.torque (θ t) - S.inertia • ∂ₜ (∂ₜ θ) t

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.equationOfMotion_iff_gradLagrangian_zero
entries.docstring:
For a smooth lift of the angle the equation of motion of the simple pendulum holds if and
  only if the variational derivative of the action vanishes: the smooth motions of the pendulum
  are the critical points of its action.
entries.snippet:
lemma equationOfMotion_iff_gradLagrangian_zero (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) :
    S.EquationOfMotion θ ↔ S.gradLagrangian θ = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.isSolution_iff
entries.docstring:
A lift of the angle is a solution of the simple pendulum if and only if it is smooth and the
  variational derivative of the action vanishes along it.
entries.snippet:
lemma isSolution_iff (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.IsSolution θ ↔ ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ ∧ S.gradLagrangian θ = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.energy_conservation_of_equationOfMotion
entries.docstring:
Along a smooth lift of the angle satisfying the equation of motion the time derivative of
  the energy of the simple pendulum vanishes.
entries.snippet:
lemma energy_conservation_of_equationOfMotion (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) (h : S.EquationOfMotion θ) : ∂ₜ (S.energy θ) = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.energy_conservation_of_equationOfMotion'
entries.docstring:
Along a smooth lift of the angle satisfying the equation of motion the energy of the simple
  pendulum at any time is equal to its initial value.
entries.snippet:
lemma energy_conservation_of_equationOfMotion' (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) (h : S.EquationOfMotion θ) (t : Time) :
    S.energy θ t = S.energy θ 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.IsSolution.energy_eq
entries.docstring:
The energy of the simple pendulum along a solution at any time is equal to its initial
  value.
entries.snippet:
lemma IsSolution.energy_eq {S : SimplePendulum} {θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)}
    (h : S.IsSolution θ) (t : Time) : S.energy θ t = S.energy θ 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.equationOfMotion_const_zero
entries.docstring:
The constant lift at the angle `0` — the bob hanging at rest at the bottom of its swing —
  satisfies the equation of motion of the simple pendulum.
entries.snippet:
lemma equationOfMotion_const_zero :
    S.EquationOfMotion (fun _ => (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.isSolution_const_zero
entries.docstring:
The hanging equilibrium is a solution of the simple pendulum: the constant lift at the angle
  `0` is smooth and satisfies the equation of motion. It is the simplest explicit solution of the
  pendulum.
entries.snippet: lemma isSolution_const_zero : S.IsSolution (fun _ => 0)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.equationOfMotion_const_pi
entries.docstring:
The constant lift at the angle `π` — the bob balanced directly above the pivot — satisfies
  the equation of motion of the simple pendulum.
entries.snippet:
lemma equationOfMotion_const_pi :
    S.EquationOfMotion (fun _ => EuclideanSpace.single 0 Real.pi)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.isSolution_const_pi
entries.docstring:
The inverted equilibrium is a solution of the simple pendulum: the constant lift at the
  angle `π` is smooth and satisfies the equation of motion.
entries.snippet: lemma isSolution_const_pi : S.IsSolution (fun _ => EuclideanSpace.single 0 Real.pi)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.equationOfMotion_const_iff
entries.docstring:
A constant lift satisfies the equation of motion of the simple pendulum if and only if the
  sine of its angle vanishes — classically, the angles straight down and straight up: the
  constant solutions are exactly the equilibria.
entries.snippet:
lemma equationOfMotion_const_iff (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.EquationOfMotion (fun _ => x) ↔ Real.sin (x 0) = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.separatrixEnergy
entries.docstring:
The separatrix energy of the simple pendulum is `2 m g ℓ`, the energy of the inverted
  equilibrium. It is the threshold separating the two regimes of the motion, libration below it
  and rotation above it.
entries.snippet: def separatrixEnergy : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.separatrixEnergy_eq
entries.docstring: The separatrix energy of the simple pendulum, written out.
entries.snippet: lemma separatrixEnergy_eq : S.separatrixEnergy = 2 * (S.m * S.g * S.ℓ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.separatrixEnergy_pos
entries.docstring: The separatrix energy of the simple pendulum is positive.
entries.snippet: lemma separatrixEnergy_pos : 0 < S.separatrixEnergy

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.energy_const_pi
entries.docstring:
The energy of the simple pendulum along the inverted equilibrium is the separatrix energy:
  the bob balanced at the top has no kinetic energy and the full potential energy `2 m g ℓ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma energy_const_pi :
    S.energy (fun _ => EuclideanSpace.single 0 Real.pi) = fun _ => S.separatrixEnergy

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.kineticEnergy_nonneg
entries.docstring: The kinetic energy of the simple pendulum is non-negative along every lift of the angle.
entries.snippet:
lemma kineticEnergy_nonneg (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (t : Time) :
    0 ≤ S.kineticEnergy θ t

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.inertia_mul_inner_deriv_le
entries.docstring:
The moment of inertia times the square of the angular speed, `I θ̇²`, is at most twice the
  total energy, along every lift of the angle.
entries.snippet:
lemma inertia_mul_inner_deriv_le (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (t : Time) :
    S.inertia * ⟪∂ₜ θ t, ∂ₜ θ t⟫_ℝ ≤ 2 * S.energy θ t

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.potentialEnergy_le_energy
entries.docstring:
The potential energy of the simple pendulum is at most the total energy along every lift of
  the angle.
entries.snippet:
lemma potentialEnergy_le_energy (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (t : Time) :
    S.potentialEnergy (θ t) ≤ S.energy θ t

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.neg_one_lt_cos_of_energy_lt
entries.docstring:
Libration: along a smooth lift of the angle satisfying the equation of motion, with energy
  below the separatrix energy, the cosine of the angle stays strictly above `-1` — the bob
  never reaches the top of the swing.
entries.snippet:
lemma neg_one_lt_cos_of_energy_lt (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) (h : S.EquationOfMotion θ)
    (hE : S.energy θ 0 < S.separatrixEnergy) (t : Time) : -1 < Real.cos (θ t 0)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.deriv_ne_zero_of_energy_gt
entries.docstring:
Rotation: along a smooth lift of the angle satisfying the equation of motion, with energy
  above the separatrix energy, the angular velocity never vanishes — the bob never halts.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_ne_zero_of_energy_gt (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) (h : S.EquationOfMotion θ)
    (hE : S.separatrixEnergy < S.energy θ 0) (t : Time) : ∂ₜ θ t ≠ 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.potentialEnergy_eq_energy_of_deriv_eq_zero
entries.docstring:
Turning points: along a smooth lift of the angle satisfying the equation of motion, at an
  instant where the angular velocity vanishes, the potential energy equals the conserved total
  energy.
entries.snippet:
lemma potentialEnergy_eq_energy_of_deriv_eq_zero (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) (h : S.EquationOfMotion θ) (t : Time) (h0 : ∂ₜ θ t = 0) :
    S.potentialEnergy (θ t) = S.energy θ 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace
entries.docstring:
The configuration space of the planar simple pendulum: the angle of the rod from the downward
  vertical, modulo `2π`.
entries.snippet:
structure ConfigurationSpace where
  angle : Real.Angle

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.ext
entries.docstring: Two configurations are equal precisely when their angles are equal.
entries.snippet:
@[ext]
lemma ext {p q : ConfigurationSpace} (h : p.angle = q.angle) : p = q

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.angleEquiv
entries.docstring: The identification of the configuration space with `Real.Angle`.
entries.snippet: def angleEquiv : ConfigurationSpace ≃ Real.Angle where

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.instTopologicalSpace
entries.docstring: The topology of the configuration space, induced from `Real.Angle`.
entries.snippet: instance instTopologicalSpace : TopologicalSpace ConfigurationSpace

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.angleHomeomorph
entries.docstring: The identification with `Real.Angle` as a homeomorphism.
entries.snippet: def angleHomeomorph : ConfigurationSpace ≃ₜ Real.Angle where

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.toCircle
entries.docstring: The point of the unit circle `e^{iθ}` corresponding to a configuration at angle `θ`.
entries.snippet: def toCircle (q : ConfigurationSpace) : Circle

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.circleHomeomorph
entries.docstring: The identification of the configuration space with the unit circle.
entries.snippet: def circleHomeomorph : ConfigurationSpace ≃ₜ Circle

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.circleHomeomorph_apply
entries.docstring: The identification with the unit circle is given by `ConfigurationSpace.toCircle`.
entries.snippet: lemma circleHomeomorph_apply (q : ConfigurationSpace) : circleHomeomorph q = q.toCircle

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.ofCircle
entries.docstring: The configuration corresponding to a point of the unit circle.
entries.snippet: def ofCircle : Circle → ConfigurationSpace

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.toCircle_ofCircle
entries.docstring:
The point of the unit circle of the configuration attached to a point of the unit circle is
  that point.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toCircle_ofCircle (z : Circle) : (ofCircle z).toCircle = z

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.ofCircle_toCircle
entries.docstring:
The configuration attached to the point of the unit circle of a configuration is that
  configuration.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofCircle_toCircle (q : ConfigurationSpace) : ofCircle q.toCircle = q

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.instT2Space
entries.docstring: The configuration space is Hausdorff, being homeomorphic to the unit circle.
entries.snippet: instance instT2Space : T2Space ConfigurationSpace

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.instCompactSpace
entries.docstring: The configuration space is compact, being homeomorphic to the unit circle.
entries.snippet: instance instCompactSpace : CompactSpace ConfigurationSpace

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.instSecondCountableTopology
entries.docstring: The configuration space is second countable, being homeomorphic to the unit circle.
entries.snippet: instance instSecondCountableTopology : SecondCountableTopology ConfigurationSpace

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.instChartedSpace
entries.docstring:
The charts of the configuration space: the identification with the unit circle followed by a
  chart of the circle.
entries.snippet: instance instChartedSpace : ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) ConfigurationSpace where

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.chartAt_eq
entries.docstring:
The chart at a configuration is the identification with the unit circle followed by the chart
  of the circle at the corresponding point.
entries.snippet:
lemma chartAt_eq (q : ConfigurationSpace) :
    chartAt (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q =
      circleHomeomorph.toOpenPartialHomeomorph.trans
        (chartAt (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q.toCircle)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.chartAt_source
entries.docstring:
The domain of the chart at a configuration is the preimage under the identification with the
  unit circle of the domain of the chart of the circle at the corresponding point.
entries.snippet:
lemma chartAt_source (q : ConfigurationSpace) :
    (chartAt (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q).source =
      circleHomeomorph ⁻¹' (chartAt (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q.toCircle).source

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.chartAt_target
entries.docstring:
The codomain of the chart at a configuration is the codomain of the chart of the circle at the
  corresponding point.
entries.snippet:
lemma chartAt_target (q : ConfigurationSpace) :
    (chartAt (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q).target =
      (chartAt (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q.toCircle).target

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.instIsManifold
entries.docstring:
The configuration space is an analytic manifold: every change of charts is a change of charts
  of the unit circle.
entries.snippet: instance instIsManifold : IsManifold (𝓡 1) ω ConfigurationSpace where

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.ofAngle
entries.docstring: The configuration at angle `θ` (measured from the downward vertical).
entries.snippet: def ofAngle (θ : ℝ) : ConfigurationSpace

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.ofAngle_angle
entries.docstring: The angle of the configuration at angle `θ` is `θ` modulo `2π`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofAngle_angle (θ : ℝ) : (ofAngle θ).angle = θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.ofAngle_add_two_pi
entries.docstring: Adding a full turn to the angle leaves the configuration unchanged.
entries.snippet: lemma ofAngle_add_two_pi (θ : ℝ) : ofAngle (θ + 2 * Real.pi) = ofAngle θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.ofAngle_periodic
entries.docstring: The angular lift is periodic with period `2π`.
entries.snippet: lemma ofAngle_periodic : Function.Periodic ofAngle (2 * Real.pi)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.ofAngle_eq_iff
entries.docstring:
Two angles describe the same configuration exactly when they differ by a whole number of
  turns.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofAngle_eq_iff (θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ) :
    ofAngle θ₁ = ofAngle θ₂ ↔ ∃ n : ℤ, θ₂ = θ₁ + n * (2 * Real.pi)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.ofAngle_surjective
entries.docstring: Every configuration is the configuration at some real angle: the lift is surjective.
entries.snippet: lemma ofAngle_surjective : Function.Surjective ofAngle

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.continuous_ofAngle
entries.docstring: The angular lift is continuous.
entries.snippet:
@[fun_prop]
lemma continuous_ofAngle : Continuous ofAngle

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.isCoveringMap_ofAngle
entries.docstring: The angular lift is a covering map.
entries.snippet: lemma isCoveringMap_ofAngle : IsCoveringMap ofAngle

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.toCircle_ofAngle
entries.docstring: The configuration at angle `θ` corresponds to the point `e^{iθ}` of the unit circle.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toCircle_ofAngle (θ : ℝ) : (ofAngle θ).toCircle = Circle.exp θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.ofCircle_circleExp
entries.docstring: The configuration of a point `e^{iθ}` of the unit circle is `ofAngle θ`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofCircle_circleExp (θ : ℝ) : ofCircle (Circle.exp θ) = ofAngle θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.contMDiff_ofAngle
entries.docstring:
The angular lift is analytic: read in the charts pulled back from the circle it is
  `Circle.exp`.
entries.snippet: lemma contMDiff_ofAngle : ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) (𝓡 1) ω ofAngle

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.cos
entries.docstring: The cosine of the angle of a configuration.
entries.snippet: def cos (q : ConfigurationSpace) : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.sin
entries.docstring: The sine of the angle of a configuration.
entries.snippet: def sin (q : ConfigurationSpace) : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.cos_angle
entries.docstring: The cosine of a configuration is the cosine of its angle.
entries.snippet: lemma cos_angle (q : ConfigurationSpace) : q.cos = Real.Angle.cos q.angle

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.sin_angle
entries.docstring: The sine of a configuration is the sine of its angle.
entries.snippet: lemma sin_angle (q : ConfigurationSpace) : q.sin = Real.Angle.sin q.angle

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.cos_ofAngle
entries.docstring: The cosine of the configuration at angle `θ` is `cos θ`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma cos_ofAngle (θ : ℝ) : (ofAngle θ).cos = Real.cos θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.sin_ofAngle
entries.docstring: The sine of the configuration at angle `θ` is `sin θ`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma sin_ofAngle (θ : ℝ) : (ofAngle θ).sin = Real.sin θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.cos_sq_add_sin_sq
entries.docstring: The Pythagorean identity for the angle of a configuration.
entries.snippet: lemma cos_sq_add_sin_sq (q : ConfigurationSpace) : q.cos ^ 2 + q.sin ^ 2 = 1

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.continuous_cos
entries.docstring: The cosine of the angle depends continuously on the configuration.
entries.snippet:
@[fun_prop]
lemma continuous_cos : Continuous (cos : ConfigurationSpace → ℝ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.continuous_sin
entries.docstring: The sine of the angle depends continuously on the configuration.
entries.snippet:
@[fun_prop]
lemma continuous_sin : Continuous (sin : ConfigurationSpace → ℝ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.toSpace
entries.docstring:
The position of the bob in the plane, for a rod of length `ℓ`. `ℓ` is not assumed positive; the
  bob is at distance `|ℓ|` from the pivot.
entries.snippet: def toSpace (ℓ : ℝ) (q : ConfigurationSpace) : Space 2

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.toSpace_apply_zero
entries.docstring: The horizontal coordinate of the bob, `ℓ * q.sin`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toSpace_apply_zero (ℓ : ℝ) (q : ConfigurationSpace) :
    toSpace ℓ q 0 = ℓ * q.sin

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.toSpace_apply_one
entries.docstring: The vertical coordinate of the bob, `-(ℓ * q.cos)`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toSpace_apply_one (ℓ : ℝ) (q : ConfigurationSpace) :
    toSpace ℓ q 1 = -(ℓ * q.cos)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.toSpace_ofAngle
entries.docstring: The position of the bob for the configuration at angle `θ`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toSpace_ofAngle (ℓ θ : ℝ) :
    toSpace ℓ (ofAngle θ) = ⟨![ℓ * Real.sin θ, -ℓ * Real.cos θ]⟩

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.toSpace_norm
entries.docstring: The rod-length constraint: the bob is at distance `|ℓ|` from the pivot.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toSpace_norm (ℓ : ℝ) (q : ConfigurationSpace) : ‖toSpace ℓ q‖ = |ℓ|

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.continuous_toSpace
entries.docstring: The position of the bob depends continuously on the configuration.
entries.snippet:
@[fun_prop]
lemma continuous_toSpace (ℓ : ℝ) : Continuous (toSpace ℓ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.toSpace_injective
entries.docstring: For a rod of nonzero length the configuration is determined by the position of the bob.
entries.snippet: lemma toSpace_injective {ℓ : ℝ} (hℓ : ℓ ≠ 0) : Function.Injective (toSpace ℓ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ConfigurationSpace.toSpace_isClosedEmbedding
entries.docstring: For `ℓ ≠ 0` the position map is a closed embedding of the configuration circle.
entries.snippet: lemma toSpace_isClosedEmbedding {ℓ : ℝ} (hℓ : ℓ ≠ 0) : Topology.IsClosedEmbedding (toSpace ℓ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.spaceTrajectory
entries.docstring:
The position of the bob in the plane along the trajectory described by a lift `θ` of the
  angle, for the pendulum `S`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def spaceTrajectory (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) : Time → Space 2

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.spaceTrajectory_eq
entries.docstring:
Along the trajectory described by a lift `θ` of the angle the bob of the pendulum `S` is at
  `(ℓ sin (θ t 0), -ℓ cos (θ t 0))`.
entries.snippet:
lemma spaceTrajectory_eq (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.spaceTrajectory θ = fun t => ⟨![S.ℓ * Real.sin (θ t 0), -S.ℓ * Real.cos (θ t 0)]⟩

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.spaceTrajectory_apply_zero
entries.docstring: The horizontal position of the bob along a lifted trajectory is `ℓ sin (θ t 0)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma spaceTrajectory_apply_zero (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (t : Time) :
    S.spaceTrajectory θ t 0 = S.ℓ * Real.sin (θ t 0)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.spaceTrajectory_apply_one
entries.docstring:
The vertical position of the bob along a lifted trajectory is `-ℓ cos (θ t 0)`, the pivot
  being the origin and the second axis pointing upwards.
entries.snippet:
lemma spaceTrajectory_apply_one (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (t : Time) :
    S.spaceTrajectory θ t 1 = -S.ℓ * Real.cos (θ t 0)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.norm_spaceTrajectory
entries.docstring:
The rod-length constraint along a lifted trajectory: the bob of the pendulum `S` stays at
  distance `ℓ` from the pivot, the length of the rod being positive.
entries.snippet:
lemma norm_spaceTrajectory (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (t : Time) :
    ‖S.spaceTrajectory θ t‖ = S.ℓ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.deriv_sin_coord
entries.docstring:
The time derivative of the sine of the angle read from a lift is the cosine of the angle
  times the angular velocity.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_sin_coord (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hθ : Differentiable ℝ θ)
    (t : Time) : ∂ₜ (fun s => Real.sin (θ s 0)) t = Real.cos (θ t 0) * (∂ₜ θ t) 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.deriv_cos_coord
entries.docstring:
The time derivative of the cosine of the angle read from a lift is minus the sine of the
  angle times the angular velocity.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_cos_coord (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hθ : Differentiable ℝ θ)
    (t : Time) : ∂ₜ (fun s => Real.cos (θ s 0)) t = -Real.sin (θ t 0) * (∂ₜ θ t) 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.differentiable_spaceTrajectory
entries.docstring:
Along a differentiable lift of the angle the position of the bob is differentiable in
  time.
entries.snippet:
@[fun_prop]
lemma differentiable_spaceTrajectory (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hθ : Differentiable ℝ θ) : Differentiable ℝ (S.spaceTrajectory θ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.deriv_spaceTrajectory
entries.docstring:
The velocity of the bob along a differentiable lift `θ` of the angle is
  `(ℓ cos (θ t 0), ℓ sin (θ t 0))` times the angular velocity: the vector tangent to the circle
  of radius `ℓ` at the position of the bob.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_spaceTrajectory (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hθ : Differentiable ℝ θ)
    (t : Time) :
    ∂ₜ (S.spaceTrajectory θ) t =
      ⟨![S.ℓ * Real.cos (θ t 0) * (∂ₜ θ t) 0, S.ℓ * Real.sin (θ t 0) * (∂ₜ θ t) 0]⟩

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.norm_sq_deriv_spaceTrajectory
entries.docstring: The square of the speed of the bob along a differentiable lift of the angle is `ℓ² θ̇²`.
entries.snippet:
lemma norm_sq_deriv_spaceTrajectory (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hθ : Differentiable ℝ θ) (t : Time) :
    ‖∂ₜ (S.spaceTrajectory θ) t‖ ^ 2 = S.ℓ ^ 2 * ((∂ₜ θ t) 0) ^ 2

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.kineticEnergy_eq_space
entries.docstring:
The chart kinetic energy of the pendulum along a differentiable lift of the angle is the
  kinetic energy of the bob in physical space.
entries.snippet:
lemma kineticEnergy_eq_space (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hθ : Differentiable ℝ θ)
    (t : Time) :
    S.kineticEnergy θ t = (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * S.m * ‖∂ₜ (S.spaceTrajectory θ) t‖ ^ 2

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.potentialEnergy_eq_height
entries.docstring:
The chart potential energy of the pendulum is the gravitational potential of the bob in
  physical space, normalized to vanish at the bottom of the swing: the height of the bob above
  the bottom is its vertical position plus `ℓ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma potentialEnergy_eq_height (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (t : Time) :
    S.potentialEnergy (θ t) = S.m * S.g * (S.spaceTrajectory θ t 1 + S.ℓ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.lagrangian_eq_space
entries.docstring:
The chart Lagrangian of the pendulum along a differentiable lift of the angle is the
  constrained Lagrangian of the bob in physical space: the kinetic energy of the point mass
  minus its gravitational potential.
entries.snippet:
lemma lagrangian_eq_space (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hθ : Differentiable ℝ θ)
    (t : Time) :
    S.lagrangian t (θ t) (∂ₜ θ t) =
      (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * S.m * ‖∂ₜ (S.spaceTrajectory θ) t‖ ^ 2
        - S.m * S.g * (S.spaceTrajectory θ t 1 + S.ℓ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.energy_eq_space
entries.docstring:
The chart energy of the pendulum along a differentiable lift of the angle is the total
  energy of the bob in physical space: the kinetic energy of the point mass plus its
  gravitational potential.
entries.snippet:
lemma energy_eq_space (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hθ : Differentiable ℝ θ)
    (t : Time) :
    S.energy θ t =
      (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * S.m * ‖∂ₜ (S.spaceTrajectory θ) t‖ ^ 2
        + S.m * S.g * (S.spaceTrajectory θ t 1 + S.ℓ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.Trajectory
entries.docstring: A trajectory of the pendulum: a curve in the configuration space.
entries.snippet: abbrev Trajectory

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.Trajectory.ofLift
entries.docstring: The trajectory on the circle described by a lift `θ` of the angle.
entries.snippet: def ofLift (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) : Trajectory

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.Trajectory.ofLift_apply
entries.docstring:
At time `t` the trajectory described by a lift `θ` of the angle is the configuration at
  angle `θ t 0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofLift_apply (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (t : Time) :
    ofLift θ t = ConfigurationSpace.ofAngle (θ t 0)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.Trajectory.ofLift_eq_iff
entries.docstring:
Two lifts of the angle describe the same trajectory exactly when at each time they differ by
  a whole number of turns.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofLift_eq_iff (θ₁ θ₂ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    ofLift θ₁ = ofLift θ₂ ↔ ∀ t, ∃ n : ℤ, θ₂ t 0 = θ₁ t 0 + n * (2 * Real.pi)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.Trajectory.ofLift_add_int_mul_two_pi
entries.docstring:
Shifting a lift of the angle by a whole number of turns leaves the described trajectory
  unchanged.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofLift_add_int_mul_two_pi (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (n : ℤ) :
    ofLift (fun t => θ t + (n * (2 * Real.pi)) • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) = ofLift θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.Trajectory.continuous_ofLift
entries.docstring: The trajectory described by a continuous lift of the angle is continuous.
entries.snippet:
lemma continuous_ofLift {θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)} (hθ : Continuous θ) :
    Continuous (ofLift θ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.Trajectory.contMDiff_ofLift
entries.docstring:
The trajectory described by a `C^n` lift of the angle is a `C^n` curve in the configuration
  circle.
entries.snippet:
lemma contMDiff_ofLift {n : WithTop ℕ∞} {θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)}
    (hθ : ContDiff ℝ n θ) : ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, Time) (𝓡 1) n (ofLift θ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.Trajectory.toSpace
entries.docstring: The physical position of the bob along a trajectory, over time, for a rod of length `ℓ`.
entries.snippet: def toSpace (ℓ : ℝ) (γ : Trajectory) (t : Time) : Space 2

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.Trajectory.toSpace_ofLift
entries.docstring:
Along the trajectory described by a lift `θ` of the angle the bob is at
  `(ℓ sin (θ t 0), -ℓ cos (θ t 0))`.
entries.snippet:
lemma toSpace_ofLift (ℓ : ℝ) (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (t : Time) :
    toSpace ℓ (ofLift θ) t = ⟨![ℓ * Real.sin (θ t 0), -ℓ * Real.cos (θ t 0)]⟩

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.Trajectory.norm_toSpace
entries.docstring:
The rod-length constraint along a trajectory: the bob stays at distance `|ℓ|` from the
  pivot.
entries.snippet: lemma norm_toSpace (ℓ : ℝ) (γ : Trajectory) (t : Time) : ‖toSpace ℓ γ t‖ = |ℓ|

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.Trajectory.continuous_toSpace
entries.docstring:
The physical position of the bob along a continuous trajectory depends continuously on the
  time.
entries.snippet:
lemma continuous_toSpace (ℓ : ℝ) {γ : Trajectory} (hγ : Continuous γ) :
    Continuous (toSpace ℓ γ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.canonicalMomentum
entries.docstring:
The canonical momentum of the simple pendulum, `p = ∂L/∂θ̇ = I θ̇`, as a linear
  equivalence between velocities and momenta in the angular chart.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def canonicalMomentum (t : Time) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) ≃ₗ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) where

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.canonicalMomentum_eq
entries.docstring:
The canonical momentum of the simple pendulum is the angular momentum `I θ̇` about the
  pivot.
entries.snippet:
lemma canonicalMomentum_eq (t : Time) (x v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.canonicalMomentum t x v = S.inertia • v

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.hamiltonian
entries.docstring:
The Hamiltonian of the simple pendulum as a function of time, momentum and angle: the
  Legendre transform `H(t, p, θ) = ⟪p, θ̇⟫ - L(t, θ, θ̇)` of the Lagrangian, the angular
  velocity `θ̇` being recovered from the momentum by inverting the canonical momentum.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def hamiltonian (t : Time) (p x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.hamiltonian_eq
entries.docstring:
The Hamiltonian of the simple pendulum is the kinetic energy written in terms of the
  momentum, `½ (1/I) ‖p‖²`, plus the potential energy.
entries.snippet:
lemma hamiltonian_eq :
    S.hamiltonian = fun _ p x =>
      (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * (1 / S.inertia) * ⟪p, p⟫_ℝ + S.potentialEnergy x

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.hamiltonian_contDiff
entries.docstring:
The Hamiltonian of the simple pendulum is a smooth function of the time, the momentum and
  the angle jointly.
entries.snippet:
@[fun_prop]
lemma hamiltonian_contDiff (n : WithTop ℕ∞) : ContDiff ℝ n ↿S.hamiltonian

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.gradient_hamiltonian_position_eq
entries.docstring:
The gradient of the Hamiltonian of the simple pendulum in the angle is the gradient of the
  potential energy, that is minus the torque.
entries.snippet:
lemma gradient_hamiltonian_position_eq (t : Time) (x p : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    gradient (S.hamiltonian t p) x = gradient S.potentialEnergy x

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.gradient_hamiltonian_momentum_eq
entries.docstring:
The gradient of the Hamiltonian of the simple pendulum in the momentum is the angular
  velocity `(1/I) p` recovered from the momentum.
entries.snippet:
lemma gradient_hamiltonian_momentum_eq (t : Time) (x p : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    gradient (S.hamiltonian t · x) p = (1 / S.inertia) • p

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.hamiltonian_eq_energy
entries.docstring:
Along any lift of the angle, the Hamiltonian of the simple pendulum evaluated on the
  canonical momentum of the lift is the energy of the lift. This holds whether or not the lift
  satisfies the equation of motion.
entries.snippet:
lemma hamiltonian_eq_energy (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    (fun t => S.hamiltonian t (S.canonicalMomentum t (θ t) (∂ₜ θ t)) (θ t)) = S.energy θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.hamiltonEqOp
entries.docstring:
The Hamilton-equations operator of the Hamiltonian of the simple pendulum, on
  momentum-angle phase space; its vanishing is equivalent to Hamilton's equations for the
  momentum and the angle.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def hamiltonEqOp (p θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.equationOfMotion_iff_hamiltonEqOp_eq_zero
entries.docstring:
For a smooth lift of the angle the equation of motion of the simple pendulum holds if and
  only if Hamilton's equations hold for the lift and its canonical momentum, that is if and
  only if the Hamilton-equations operator vanishes on the pair.
entries.snippet:
lemma equationOfMotion_iff_hamiltonEqOp_eq_zero (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) :
    S.EquationOfMotion θ ↔
      S.hamiltonEqOp (fun t => S.canonicalMomentum t (θ t) (∂ₜ θ t)) θ = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.equationOfMotion_tfae
entries.snippet:
lemma equationOfMotion_tfae (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) :
    List.TFAE [S.EquationOfMotion θ,
      ∀ t, ∂ₜ (∂ₜ θ) t 0 + S.ω ^ 2 * Real.sin (θ t 0) = 0,
      S.hamiltonEqOp (fun t => S.canonicalMomentum t (θ t) (∂ₜ θ t)) θ = 0,
      (δ (q':=θ), ∫ t, S.lagrangian t (q' t) (fderiv ℝ q' t 1)) = 0,
      (δ (pq':= fun t => (S.canonicalMomentum t (θ t) (∂ₜ θ t), θ t)),
        ∫ t, ⟪(pq' t).1, ∂ₜ (Prod.snd ∘ pq') t⟫_ℝ -
          S.hamiltonian t (pq' t).1 (pq' t).2) = 0]

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.potentialEnergy_add_int_mul_two_pi
entries.docstring:
The potential energy of the simple pendulum is invariant under shifting the angle by a
  whole number of turns.
entries.snippet:
lemma potentialEnergy_add_int_mul_two_pi (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (n : ℤ) :
    S.potentialEnergy (x + (n * (2 * Real.pi)) • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) =
      S.potentialEnergy x

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.torque_add_int_mul_two_pi
entries.docstring:
The torque of the simple pendulum is invariant under shifting the angle by a whole number
  of turns.
entries.snippet:
lemma torque_add_int_mul_two_pi (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (n : ℤ) :
    S.torque (x + (n * (2 * Real.pi)) • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) = S.torque x

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.kineticEnergy_add_const
entries.docstring:
The kinetic energy of the simple pendulum along a lift of the angle is invariant under
  shifting the lift by any constant: the shift drops out of the velocity.
entries.snippet:
lemma kineticEnergy_add_const (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (c : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.kineticEnergy (fun t => θ t + c) = S.kineticEnergy θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.energy_add_int_mul_two_pi
entries.docstring:
The energy of the simple pendulum along a lift of the angle is invariant under shifting the
  lift by a whole number of turns: A.1 supplies the invariance of the potential energy, and the
  velocity is unchanged by a constant shift.
entries.snippet:
lemma energy_add_int_mul_two_pi (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (n : ℤ) :
    S.energy (fun t => θ t + (n * (2 * Real.pi)) • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) =
      S.energy θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.equationOfMotion_add_int_mul_two_pi
entries.docstring:
A lift of the angle shifted by a whole number of turns satisfies the equation of motion of
  the simple pendulum if and only if the lift itself does.
entries.snippet:
lemma equationOfMotion_add_int_mul_two_pi (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (n : ℤ) :
    S.EquationOfMotion (fun t => θ t + (n * (2 * Real.pi)) • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) ↔
      S.EquationOfMotion θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.isSolution_add_int_mul_two_pi
entries.docstring:
A lift of the angle shifted by a whole number of turns is a solution of the simple pendulum
  if and only if the lift itself is.
entries.snippet:
lemma isSolution_add_int_mul_two_pi (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (n : ℤ) :
    S.IsSolution (fun t => θ t + (n * (2 * Real.pi)) • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) ↔
      S.IsSolution θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.ofAngle_add_int_mul_two_pi_coord
entries.docstring:
A lift of the angle and its shift by a whole number of turns describe the same
  configuration of the simple pendulum.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofAngle_add_int_mul_two_pi_coord (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (n : ℤ) :
    ConfigurationSpace.ofAngle
        ((x + (n * (2 * Real.pi)) • EuclideanSpace.single (0 : Fin 1) (1 : ℝ)) 0) =
      ConfigurationSpace.ofAngle (x 0)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.toHarmonicOscillator
entries.docstring:
The harmonic oscillator to which the pendulum linearizes: mass `I = m ℓ²`, spring
  constant `m g ℓ`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def toHarmonicOscillator : HarmonicOscillator where

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.toHarmonicOscillator_m
entries.docstring:
The mass of the harmonic oscillator associated to the simple pendulum is the moment of
  inertia `I = m ℓ²` of the pendulum about its pivot.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toHarmonicOscillator_m : S.toHarmonicOscillator.m = S.inertia

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.toHarmonicOscillator_k
entries.docstring:
The spring constant of the harmonic oscillator associated to the simple pendulum is
  `m g ℓ`, the coefficient of the linearized torque.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toHarmonicOscillator_k : S.toHarmonicOscillator.k = S.m * S.g * S.ℓ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.toHarmonicOscillator_ω
entries.docstring:
The angular frequency of the harmonic oscillator associated to the simple pendulum is the
  angular frequency `ω = √(g/ℓ)` of the small oscillations of the pendulum.
entries.snippet: lemma toHarmonicOscillator_ω : S.toHarmonicOscillator.ω = S.ω

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.LinearizedEquationOfMotion
entries.docstring:
The linearized equation of motion `θ̈ + ω² θ = 0` of the simple pendulum, the small-angle
  form of the equation of motion, in which the torque is replaced by its linearization at the
  bottom of the swing.
entries.snippet: def LinearizedEquationOfMotion (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) : Prop

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.linearizedEquationOfMotion_iff_newton
entries.docstring:
The linearized equation of motion in the rotational form of Newton's second law: at every
  instant the rate of change `I θ̈` of the angular momentum equals the force `-m g ℓ θ` of the
  associated harmonic oscillator. No smoothness is required: the two pointwise equations differ
  by the nonzero factor `I`.
entries.snippet:
lemma linearizedEquationOfMotion_iff_newton (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.LinearizedEquationOfMotion θ ↔
      ∀ t, S.inertia • ∂ₜ (∂ₜ θ) t = S.toHarmonicOscillator.force (θ t)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.linearizedEquationOfMotion_iff
entries.docstring:
For a smooth lift of the angle, the linearized equation of motion of the simple pendulum is
  the equation of motion of the associated harmonic oscillator. The oscillator's equation of
  motion is the vanishing of the variational gradient of its action, which is totalized;
  smoothness is the regularity under which that variational description agrees with the pointwise
  one. The smoothness-free pointwise content is `linearizedEquationOfMotion_iff_newton`.
entries.snippet:
lemma linearizedEquationOfMotion_iff (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) :
    S.LinearizedEquationOfMotion θ ↔ S.toHarmonicOscillator.EquationOfMotion θ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.fderiv_torque_zero_apply
entries.docstring:
The derivative of the torque at the hanging equilibrium is the force of the associated
  harmonic oscillator: `(Dτ)(0) v = -m g ℓ v`. Linearizing the pendulum is differentiating
  its torque at the equilibrium.
entries.snippet:
lemma fderiv_torque_zero_apply (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    fderiv ℝ S.torque 0 v = S.toHarmonicOscillator.force v

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.linearizedEquationOfMotion_iff_fderiv_torque
entries.docstring:
The linearized equation of motion is the equation of motion with the torque replaced by
  its derivative at the hanging equilibrium.
entries.snippet:
lemma linearizedEquationOfMotion_iff_fderiv_torque (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.LinearizedEquationOfMotion θ ↔
      ∀ t, S.inertia • ∂ₜ (∂ₜ θ) t = fderiv ℝ S.torque 0 (θ t)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.smallAngleTrajectory
entries.docstring:
The small-angle motion of the simple pendulum with initial angle `IC.x₀` and initial
  angular velocity `IC.v₀`: the trajectory of the associated harmonic oscillator with the same
  initial conditions.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def smallAngleTrajectory (IC : HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditions) :
    Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.smallAngleTrajectory_contDiff
entries.docstring: The small-angle trajectories of the simple pendulum are smooth in time.
entries.snippet:
@[fun_prop]
lemma smallAngleTrajectory_contDiff (IC : HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditions)
    {n : WithTop ℕ∞} : ContDiff ℝ n (S.smallAngleTrajectory IC)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.smallAngleTrajectory_at_zero
entries.docstring: At time `0` the small-angle trajectory passes through its initial angle.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma smallAngleTrajectory_at_zero (IC : HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditions) :
    S.smallAngleTrajectory IC 0 = IC.x₀

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.smallAngleTrajectory_velocity_at_zero
entries.docstring: At time `0` the small-angle trajectory moves with its initial angular velocity.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma smallAngleTrajectory_velocity_at_zero (IC : HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditions) :
    ∂ₜ (S.smallAngleTrajectory IC) 0 = IC.v₀

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.smallAngleTrajectory_eq
entries.docstring:
The closed form of the small-angle motion: `cos (ω t) x₀ + (sin (ω t)/ω) v₀`, the
  trajectory of the associated harmonic oscillator with its frequency read as the `ω` of the
  pendulum.
entries.snippet:
lemma smallAngleTrajectory_eq (IC : HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditions) :
    S.smallAngleTrajectory IC = fun t : Time =>
      Real.cos (S.ω * t.val) • IC.x₀ + (Real.sin (S.ω * t.val) / S.ω) • IC.v₀

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.smallAngleTrajectory_linearizedEquationOfMotion
entries.docstring:
The small-angle trajectories satisfy the linearized equation of motion: for every choice
  of initial conditions the linearized equation has a smooth solution assuming them.
entries.snippet:
lemma smallAngleTrajectory_linearizedEquationOfMotion
    (IC : HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditions) :
    S.LinearizedEquationOfMotion (S.smallAngleTrajectory IC)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.linearized_unique
entries.docstring:
Uniqueness of the small-angle motions: a smooth solution of the linearized equation of
  motion is determined by its initial angle and initial angular velocity, being the
  small-angle trajectory of those initial conditions. This is the uniqueness theorem for the
  associated harmonic oscillator, transferred through `linearizedEquationOfMotion_iff`.
entries.snippet:
lemma linearized_unique (IC : HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditions)
    (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ)
    (h : S.LinearizedEquationOfMotion θ) (h0 : θ 0 = IC.x₀) (hv : ∂ₜ θ 0 = IC.v₀) :
    θ = S.smallAngleTrajectory IC

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.releasedFromRest
entries.docstring:
The small-angle motion of the pendulum released from rest at initial angle `θ₀`: the
  cosine `θ₀ cos (ω t)` of angular frequency `ω`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def releasedFromRest (θ₀ : ℝ) : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.releasedFromRest_eq
entries.docstring:
The motion released from rest at angle `θ₀` is the small-angle trajectory of the initial
  conditions with initial angle `θ₀` and zero initial angular velocity.
entries.snippet:
lemma releasedFromRest_eq (θ₀ : ℝ) :
    S.releasedFromRest θ₀ = S.smallAngleTrajectory ⟨EuclideanSpace.single 0 θ₀, 0⟩

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.releasedFromRest_at_zero
entries.docstring: At time `0` the motion released from rest at angle `θ₀` is at the angle `θ₀`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma releasedFromRest_at_zero (θ₀ : ℝ) :
    S.releasedFromRest θ₀ 0 = EuclideanSpace.single 0 θ₀

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.releasedFromRest_velocity_at_zero
entries.docstring:
The motion released from rest at angle `θ₀` is genuinely released from rest: its angular
  velocity at time `0` vanishes.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma releasedFromRest_velocity_at_zero (θ₀ : ℝ) : ∂ₜ (S.releasedFromRest θ₀) 0 = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.releasedFromRest_linearizedEquationOfMotion
entries.docstring:
The motion released from rest at angle `θ₀` satisfies the linearized equation of
  motion.
entries.snippet:
lemma releasedFromRest_linearizedEquationOfMotion (θ₀ : ℝ) :
    S.LinearizedEquationOfMotion (S.releasedFromRest θ₀)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.smallAnglePeriod
entries.docstring:
The period `2π √(ℓ/g)` of the small oscillations of the simple pendulum: the period of the
  associated harmonic oscillator. Within the linearization it does not depend on the
  amplitude — the small oscillations are isochronous, as derived by Huygens (1673).
entries.snippet: noncomputable def smallAnglePeriod : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.smallAnglePeriod_eq_two_pi_div_ω
entries.docstring:
The period of the small oscillations is `2π/ω`, one full circle of phase at the angular
  frequency `ω` of the small oscillations.
entries.snippet: lemma smallAnglePeriod_eq_two_pi_div_ω : S.smallAnglePeriod = 2 * Real.pi / S.ω

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.smallAnglePeriod_eq
entries.docstring:
The closed form of the small-angle period: `2π √(ℓ/g)`. Neither the mass of the bob nor
  the amplitude of the swing appears.
entries.snippet: lemma smallAnglePeriod_eq : S.smallAnglePeriod = 2 * Real.pi * √(S.ℓ / S.g)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.smallAnglePeriod_pos
entries.docstring: The period of the small oscillations is positive.
entries.snippet: lemma smallAnglePeriod_pos : 0 < S.smallAnglePeriod

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.smallAngleTrajectory_periodic
entries.docstring:
The small-angle trajectories of the simple pendulum are periodic with the small-angle
  period `2π √(ℓ/g)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma smallAngleTrajectory_periodic (IC : HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditions) :
    Function.Periodic (S.smallAngleTrajectory IC) (S.smallAnglePeriod : Time)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.releasedFromRest_periodic
entries.docstring:
The motion released from rest at angle `θ₀` is periodic with the small-angle period: after
  each time `2π √(ℓ/g)` the motion returns to the angle `θ₀` with zero angular velocity.
entries.snippet:
lemma releasedFromRest_periodic (θ₀ : ℝ) :
    Function.Periodic (S.releasedFromRest θ₀) (S.smallAnglePeriod : Time)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.smallAngleTrajectory_energy
entries.docstring:
Along a small-angle trajectory the energy of the associated harmonic oscillator is the
  constant `½ (I ‖v₀‖² + m g ℓ ‖IC.x₀‖²)` fixed by the initial data: the rotational kinetic term
  of the initial angular velocity plus the potential term of the initial angle.
entries.snippet:
lemma smallAngleTrajectory_energy (IC : HarmonicOscillator.InitialConditions) :
    S.toHarmonicOscillator.energy (S.smallAngleTrajectory IC) =
      fun _ => 1 / 2 * (S.inertia * ‖IC.v₀‖ ^ 2 + S.m * S.g * S.ℓ * ‖IC.x₀‖ ^ 2)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.torque_sub_toHarmonicOscillator_force
entries.docstring:
The difference between the torque of the simple pendulum and the force of its associated
  harmonic oscillator is `m g ℓ (θ - sin θ)` times the unit vector of the angular direction:
  exactly the term the linearization discards.
entries.snippet:
lemma torque_sub_toHarmonicOscillator_force (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.torque x - S.toHarmonicOscillator.force x =
      (S.m * S.g * S.ℓ * (x 0 - Real.sin (x 0))) • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.norm_torque_sub_toHarmonicOscillator_force_le
entries.docstring:
The normed form of the cubic bound: the torque of the simple pendulum differs from the
  force of its associated harmonic oscillator by at most `m g ℓ ‖θ‖³ / 6` in norm.
entries.snippet:
lemma norm_torque_sub_toHarmonicOscillator_force_le (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    ‖S.torque x - S.toHarmonicOscillator.force x‖ ≤ S.m * S.g * S.ℓ * ‖x‖ ^ 3 / 6

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.abs_torque_add_linear_le
entries.docstring:
The torque of the simple pendulum differs from its linearization `-m g ℓ θ` by at most
  `m g ℓ |θ|³ / 6`: the error of the small-angle approximation is cubic in the angle.
entries.snippet:
lemma abs_torque_add_linear_le (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    |S.torque x 0 + S.m * S.g * S.ℓ * x 0| ≤ S.m * S.g * S.ℓ * |x 0| ^ 3 / 6

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.gradLagrangian_sub_toHarmonicOscillator
entries.docstring:
Along a smooth lift of the angle, the variational gradients of the actions of the simple
  pendulum and of its associated harmonic oscillator differ exactly by the difference between
  the torque and the linearized force: the inertial terms cancel.
entries.snippet:
lemma gradLagrangian_sub_toHarmonicOscillator (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) :
    S.gradLagrangian θ - S.toHarmonicOscillator.gradLagrangian θ =
      fun t => S.torque (θ t) - S.toHarmonicOscillator.force (θ t)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.norm_gradLagrangian_sub_toHarmonicOscillator_le
entries.docstring:
The normed form: along a smooth lift of the angle the variational gradients of the two
  actions differ at every instant by at most `m g ℓ ‖θ t‖³ / 6` — the two actions have the
  same critical-point equation to cubic accuracy in the angle.
entries.snippet:
lemma norm_gradLagrangian_sub_toHarmonicOscillator_le (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ) (t : Time) :
    ‖S.gradLagrangian θ t - S.toHarmonicOscillator.gradLagrangian θ t‖ ≤
      S.m * S.g * S.ℓ * ‖θ t‖ ^ 3 / 6

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.norm_equationOfMotion_residual_le
entries.docstring:
A motion satisfying the linearized equation of motion nearly solves the equation of motion
  of the pendulum itself: at every instant the residual `I θ̈ - τ(θ)` has norm at most
  `m g ℓ ‖θ‖³ / 6`, cubically small for small angles.
entries.snippet:
lemma norm_equationOfMotion_residual_le (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (h : S.LinearizedEquationOfMotion θ) (t : Time) :
    ‖S.inertia • ∂ₜ (∂ₜ θ) t - S.torque (θ t)‖ ≤ S.m * S.g * S.ℓ * ‖θ t‖ ^ 3 / 6

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.SimplePendulum.norm_gradLagrangian_le_of_linearizedEquationOfMotion
entries.docstring:
The variational form of the residual: a smooth motion of the linearized dynamics is a
  near-critical point of the pendulum's own action — along it the variational gradient of the
  pendulum's action is cubically small in the angle.
entries.snippet:
lemma norm_gradLagrangian_le_of_linearizedEquationOfMotion
    (θ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hθ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ)
    (h : S.LinearizedEquationOfMotion θ) (t : Time) :
    ‖S.gradLagrangian θ t‖ ≤ S.m * S.g * S.ℓ * ‖θ t‖ ^ 3 / 6

entries.name: RigidBody.inertiaTensorAbout
entries.docstring:
The inertia tensor of the rigid body about the point `p`, that is with the moments taken
about `p` rather than about the origin of the reference frame. Taking `p` to be the origin
recovers `RigidBody.inertiaTensor`, see `RigidBody.inertiaTensorAbout_zero`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def inertiaTensorAbout {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) (p : Space d) :
    Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ

entries.name: RigidBody.inertiaTensorAbout_apply
entries.docstring: The `(i, j)` entry of the inertia tensor about `p` as a moment of the mass distribution.
entries.snippet:
lemma inertiaTensorAbout_apply {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) (p : Space d) (i j : Fin d) :
    R.inertiaTensorAbout p i j = R.ρ (cmap (fun y => (if i = j then 1 else 0) *
      ∑ k : Fin d, (y k - p k) ^ 2 - (y i - p i) * (y j - p j)) (by fun_prop))

entries.name: RigidBody.inertiaTensorAbout_zero
entries.docstring: The inertia tensor about the origin is the inertia tensor.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma inertiaTensorAbout_zero {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) :
    R.inertiaTensorAbout 0 = R.inertiaTensor

entries.name: RigidBody.inertiaTensorAbout_symmetric
entries.docstring: The inertia tensor about any point is symmetric.
entries.snippet:
lemma inertiaTensorAbout_symmetric {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) (p : Space d) (i j : Fin d) :
    R.inertiaTensorAbout p i j = R.inertiaTensorAbout p j i

entries.name: RigidBody.inertiaTensorAbout_integrand_split
entries.docstring:
The integrand of the inertia tensor about `p` splits into the integrand about the centre of
mass, terms linear in the centred coordinates `y − c`, and a constant built from the
displacement `c − p`.
entries.snippet:
lemma inertiaTensorAbout_integrand_split {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) (p : Space d) (i j : Fin d) :
    cmap (fun y => (if i = j then 1 else 0) * ∑ k : Fin d, (y k - p k) ^ 2
        - (y i - p i) * (y j - p j)) (by fun_prop)
      = cmap (fun y => (if i = j then 1 else 0) * ∑ k : Fin d, (y k - R.centerOfMass k) ^ 2
            - (y i - R.centerOfMass i) * (y j - R.centerOfMass j)) (by fun_prop)
        + ∑ k : Fin d, (2 * (if i = j then 1 else 0) * (R.centerOfMass k - p k)) •
            cmap (fun y => y k - R.centerOfMass k) (by fun_prop)
        - (R.centerOfMass j - p j) • cmap (fun y => y i - R.centerOfMass i) (by fun_prop)
        - (R.centerOfMass i - p i) • cmap (fun y => y j - R.centerOfMass j) (by fun_prop)
        + ((if i = j then 1 else 0) * ∑ k : Fin d, (R.centerOfMass k - p k) ^ 2
            - (R.centerOfMass i - p i) * (R.centerOfMass j - p j)) •
          (1 : C^⊤⟮𝓘(ℝ, Space d), Space d; 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ), ℝ⟯)

entries.name: RigidBody.inertiaTensorAbout_eq_centerOfMass_add_pointMass
entries.docstring:
**The parallel-axis theorem**: the inertia tensor about a point `p` is the inertia tensor
about the centre of mass `c` plus the inertia tensor about `p` of a point particle carrying the
total mass of the body and sitting at `c`, that is `M (|c − p|² 1 − (c − p) ⊗ (c − p))`.
entries.snippet:
theorem inertiaTensorAbout_eq_centerOfMass_add_pointMass {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) (h : R.mass ≠ 0)
    (p : Space d) :
    R.inertiaTensorAbout p = R.inertiaTensorAbout R.centerOfMass
      + R.mass • (⟪R.centerOfMass - p, R.centerOfMass - p⟫_ℝ • (1 : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ)
        - Matrix.vecMulVec ⇑(R.centerOfMass - p) ⇑(R.centerOfMass - p))

entries.name: RigidBody.inertiaTensor_eq_centerOfMass_add_pointMass
entries.docstring:
The inertia tensor about the origin is the inertia tensor about the centre of mass `c` plus
`M (|c|² 1 − c ⊗ c)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma inertiaTensor_eq_centerOfMass_add_pointMass {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) (h : R.mass ≠ 0) :
    R.inertiaTensor = R.inertiaTensorAbout R.centerOfMass
      + R.mass • (⟪R.centerOfMass, R.centerOfMass⟫_ℝ • (1 : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ)
        - Matrix.vecMulVec ⇑R.centerOfMass ⇑R.centerOfMass)

entries.name: ChargeUnit.div_mul_div
entries.docstring: The unit-ratio cocycle at `ℝ≥0` (the un-coerced form of `div_mul_div_coe`).
entries.snippet: lemma div_mul_div (x y z : ChargeUnit) : (x / y) * (y / z) = x / z

entries.name: gradient_add_const
entries.docstring: Adding a constant to a function does not change its gradient.
entries.snippet:
lemma gradient_add_const {f : F → ℝ} (c : ℝ) (x : F) :
    gradient (fun y => f y + c) x = gradient f x

entries.name: gradient_const_mul
entries.docstring:
The gradient of a constant multiple of a differentiable function is the constant multiple of
the gradient.
entries.snippet:
lemma gradient_const_mul {f : F → ℝ} {x : F} (c : ℝ) (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) :
    gradient (fun y => c * f y) x = c • gradient f x

entries.name: gradient_inner_self
entries.docstring: The gradient of `y ↦ ⟪y, y⟫` at `x` is `2 • x`.
entries.snippet: lemma gradient_inner_self (x : F) : gradient (fun y : F => ⟪y, y⟫_ℝ) x = (2 : ℝ) • x

entries.name: gradient_const_mul_inner_self
entries.docstring: The gradient of `y ↦ c * ⟪y, y⟫` at `x` is `(2 * c) • x`.
entries.snippet:
lemma gradient_const_mul_inner_self (c : ℝ) (x : F) :
    gradient (fun y : F => c * ⟪y, y⟫_ℝ) x = (2 * c) • x

entries.name: gradient_coord
entries.docstring:
The gradient of the `i`-th coordinate functional on Euclidean space is the `i`-th basis
vector.
entries.snippet:
lemma gradient_coord {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (i : ι) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) :
    gradient (fun y : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι => y i) x = EuclideanSpace.single i 1

entries.name: gradient_comp_coord
entries.docstring:
Chain rule for a function of one coordinate: the gradient of `y ↦ f (y i)` at `x` is
`f' • EuclideanSpace.single i 1`, where `f'` is the derivative of `f` at `x i`.

entries.name: Function.HasTemperateGrowth.prod
entries.docstring: The finite product of functions of temperate growth is again of temperate growth.
entries.snippet:
@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma prod {ι : Type*} {s : Finset ι} {E F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedCommRing F] [NormedAlgebra ℝ F] {f : ι → E → F}
    (hf : ∀ i ∈ s, HasTemperateGrowth (f i)) : HasTemperateGrowth (∏ i ∈ s, f i)

entries.name: KroneckerDelta.generalizedKroneckerDelta_comp_perm
entries.docstring:
Simultaneously reindexing the upper and lower slots of a generalized Kronecker delta by the
same permutation leaves it unchanged.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma generalizedKroneckerDelta_comp_perm {α ι : Type} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq ι]
    [Fintype ι] (μ ν : ι → α) (e : Equiv.Perm ι) :
    generalizedKroneckerDelta (μ ∘ e) (ν ∘ e) = generalizedKroneckerDelta μ ν

entries.name: sum_generalizedKroneckerDelta_mul_snoc
entries.docstring: Symbol-level triple contraction with the free index in the last slot.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_generalizedKroneckerDelta_mul_snoc (σ τ : Fin 4) :
    ∑ h : Fin 3 → Fin 4,
        generalizedKroneckerDelta (Fin.snoc h σ) id * generalizedKroneckerDelta (Fin.snoc h τ) id =
      6 * ((kroneckerDelta σ τ : ℕ) : ℤ)

entries.name: leviCivitaSymbol
entries.docstring:
The Levi-Civita symbol on a finite index type `ι`: `leviCivitaSymbol g` is the sign
of `g` when `g : ι → ι` is a permutation, and `0` otherwise. It is the generalized
Kronecker delta of `g` against the identity, i.e. the determinant of the matrix of
Kronecker deltas `δ[g i, j]`.

For `ι = Fin d` this is the Levi-Civita symbol `ε_{i₁ ⋯ i_d}` in dimension `d`,
normalized by `ε_{0 1 ⋯ (d-1)} = 1`.
entries.snippet: def leviCivitaSymbol (g : ι → ι) : ℤ

entries.name: leviCivitaSymbol_eq_det
entries.docstring:
The Levi-Civita symbol as the determinant of the matrix of Kronecker deltas
`δ[g i, j]`.
entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivitaSymbol_eq_det (g : ι → ι) :
    leviCivitaSymbol g = Matrix.det (fun i j => ((kroneckerDelta (g i) j : ℕ) : ℤ))

entries.name: leviCivitaSymbol_id
entries.docstring: The Levi-Civita symbol of the identity, i.e. `ε_{0 1 ⋯ (d-1)}`, is `1`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma leviCivitaSymbol_id : leviCivitaSymbol (id : ι → ι) = 1

entries.name: leviCivitaSymbol_perm
entries.docstring: The Levi-Civita symbol of a permutation `σ` is the sign of `σ`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma leviCivitaSymbol_perm (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) :
    leviCivitaSymbol ⇑σ = (Equiv.Perm.sign σ : ℤ)

entries.name: leviCivitaSymbol_comp_swap
entries.docstring:
The Levi-Civita symbol is antisymmetric under transposition of two of its indices:
precomposing with the swap of two distinct index positions negates it.
entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivitaSymbol_comp_swap (g : ι → ι) {i j : ι} (hij : i ≠ j) :
    leviCivitaSymbol (g ∘ Equiv.swap i j) = - leviCivitaSymbol g

entries.name: leviCivitaSymbol_swap_comp
entries.docstring:
The Levi-Civita symbol is antisymmetric under transposition of two index values:
postcomposing with the swap of two distinct values exchanges those two values wherever
they occur and negates it.
entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivitaSymbol_swap_comp (g : ι → ι) {i j : ι} (hij : i ≠ j) :
    leviCivitaSymbol (Equiv.swap i j ∘ g) = - leviCivitaSymbol g

entries.name: leviCivitaSymbol_eq_zero_of_eq
entries.docstring:
The Levi-Civita symbol vanishes on a repeated index: if two distinct index positions
`i ≠ j` carry the same value, the symbol is zero.
entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivitaSymbol_eq_zero_of_eq {g : ι → ι} {i j : ι} (hij : i ≠ j) (h : g i = g j) :
    leviCivitaSymbol g = 0

entries.name: leviCivitaSymbol_eq_zero_of_not_injective
entries.docstring: The Levi-Civita symbol vanishes on maps which are not injective.
