entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivitaSymbol_eq_zero_of_not_injective {g : ι → ι} (h : ¬ Function.Injective g) :
    leviCivitaSymbol g = 0

entries.name: leviCivitaSymbol_eq_zero_iff
entries.docstring:
The Levi-Civita symbol vanishes exactly on maps with a repeated index, i.e. on maps
which are not injective.
entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivitaSymbol_eq_zero_iff {g : ι → ι} :
    leviCivitaSymbol g = 0 ↔ ¬ Function.Injective g

entries.name: Physlib.List.takeWhile_eraseIdx
entries.snippet:
lemma takeWhile_eraseIdx {I : Type} (P : I → Prop) [DecidablePred P] :
    (l : List I) → (i : ℕ) → (hi : ∀ (i j : Fin l.length), i < j → P (l.get j) → P (l.get i)) →
    List.takeWhile P (List.eraseIdx l i) = (List.takeWhile P l).eraseIdx i
  | [], _, h => by
    rfl
  | a :: [], 0, h => by
    simp only [List.takeWhile, List.eraseIdx_zero]
    split <;> rfl
  | a :: [], Nat.succ n, h => by
    simp only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one, List.eraseIdx_cons_succ, List.eraseIdx_nil]
    rw [List.eraseIdx_of_length_le ((List.takeWhile_sublist _).length_le.trans (by simp))]
  | a :: b :: l, 0, h => by
    simp only [List.takeWhile, List.eraseIdx_zero]
    by_cases hPb : P b
    · have hPa : P a

entries.name: OneParameterSubgroup.«instance@cdaeda53»
entries.docstring:
`NormedSpace.exp`'s API wants a `ℚ`-algebra structure (for the `1/n!` coefficients), which
isn't automatic from `NormedAlgebra ℝ E` alone; derive it once here rather than at each use site.
entries.snippet: local instance : NormedAlgebra ℚ E

entries.name: OneParameterSubgroup.exists_isUnit_intervalIntegral
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_isUnit_intervalIntegral [Nontrivial E] (U : AddChar ℝ E) (hU : Continuous U) :
    ∃ d : ℝ, 0 < d ∧ IsUnit (∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..d, U x)

entries.name: OneParameterSubgroup.mul_intervalIntegral_eq_sub
entries.docstring: Translating a one-parameter subgroup translates its interval integral.
entries.snippet:
lemma mul_intervalIntegral_eq_sub (U : AddChar ℝ E) (hU : Continuous U) (s t : ℝ) :
    U s * ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..t, U x =
      (∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..(s + t), U x) - ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..s, U x

entries.name: OneParameterSubgroup.differentiable
entries.snippet:
lemma differentiable [Nontrivial E] (U : AddChar ℝ E) (hU : Continuous U) :
    Differentiable ℝ U

entries.name: OneParameterSubgroup.apply_eq_exp_smul_deriv
entries.snippet:
lemma apply_eq_exp_smul_deriv (U : AddChar ℝ E) (hU : Continuous U) (t : ℝ) :
    U t = NormedSpace.exp (t • deriv U 0)

entries.name: OneParameterSubgroup.generator_unique
entries.docstring: Any exponential generator of a one-parameter subgroup is its derivative at zero.
entries.snippet:
lemma generator_unique (U : AddChar ℝ E) (A : E)
    (h : ∀ t : ℝ, U t = NormedSpace.exp (t • A)) : A = deriv U 0

entries.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup
entries.docstring: A norm-continuous unitary one-parameter group on a complex Hilbert space.
entries.snippet:
structure UnitaryOneParameterGroup (H : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
    [CompleteSpace H] where
  toAddChar : AddChar ℝ (H →L[ℂ] H)
  mem_unitary : ∀ t, toAddChar t ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)
  continuous : Continuous toAddChar

entries.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.«instance@c9335d72»
entries.snippet: instance : CoeFun (UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) fun _ => ℝ → (H →L[ℂ] H)

entries.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.ext
entries.snippet:
@[ext]
lemma ext {U V : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H} (h : ∀ t, U t = V t) : U = V

entries.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.apply_eq_exp_deriv
entries.snippet:
lemma apply_eq_exp_deriv (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) (t : ℝ) :
    U t = NormedSpace.exp ((t : ℂ) • deriv U 0)

entries.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.adjoint_eq
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma adjoint_eq (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) (t : ℝ) : (U t).adjoint = U (-t)

entries.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.generator
entries.docstring: The bounded self-adjoint generator of `U`, in the convention `U(t) = exp (-itA)`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def generator (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) : H →L[ℂ] H

entries.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.apply_eq_exp_generator
entries.snippet:
lemma apply_eq_exp_generator (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) (t : ℝ) :
    U t = NormedSpace.exp ((-(t : ℂ) * Complex.I) • U.generator)

entries.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.generator_unique
entries.docstring:
Any exponential generator of a unitary one-parameter group equals `U.generator`; the
uniqueness of the derivative at zero (`OneParameterSubgroup.generator_unique`) is the underlying
fact, restated here in terms of the physics convention.
entries.snippet:
lemma generator_unique (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) (A : H →L[ℂ] H)
    (h : ∀ t : ℝ, U t = NormedSpace.exp ((-(t : ℂ) * Complex.I) • A)) :
    A = U.generator

entries.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.adjoint_deriv_eq_neg
entries.snippet:
lemma adjoint_deriv_eq_neg (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) :
    (deriv U 0).adjoint = -deriv U 0

entries.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.generator_isSelfAdjoint
entries.docstring: The generator of a unitary one-parameter group is self-adjoint.
entries.snippet: lemma generator_isSelfAdjoint (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) : IsSelfAdjoint U.generator

entries.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.ofSelfAdjoint
entries.docstring: The unitary one-parameter group generated by a bounded self-adjoint operator.
entries.snippet:
def ofSelfAdjoint {A : H →L[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) :
    UnitaryOneParameterGroup H

entries.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.ofSelfAdjoint_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofSelfAdjoint_apply {A : H →L[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t : ℝ) :
    ofSelfAdjoint hA t = NormedSpace.exp ((-(t : ℂ) * Complex.I) • A)

entries.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.ofSelfAdjoint_generator
entries.docstring:
`ofSelfAdjoint` recovers `U` from its own generator: this is the defining property used to
show `stoneEquiv` is a left inverse.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofSelfAdjoint_generator (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) :
    ofSelfAdjoint U.generator_isSelfAdjoint = U

entries.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.generator_ofSelfAdjoint
entries.docstring:
The generator of `ofSelfAdjoint hA` is `A` itself: this is the defining property used to show
`stoneEquiv` is a right inverse.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma generator_ofSelfAdjoint {A : H →L[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) :
    (ofSelfAdjoint hA).generator = A

entries.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.stoneEquiv
entries.docstring:
Stone's correspondence between norm-continuous unitary one-parameter groups and bounded
self-adjoint generators.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def stoneEquiv :
    UnitaryOneParameterGroup H ≃ {A : H →L[ℂ] H // IsSelfAdjoint A} where

entries.name: Physlib.RatComplexNum.neg_I_mul_toComplexNum
entries.docstring: Multiplication by `-I` under the inclusion of `RatComplexNum` into the complex numbers.
entries.snippet:
lemma neg_I_mul_toComplexNum (a : RatComplexNum) :
    (-I) * toComplexNum a = toComplexNum (- (⟨0, 1⟩ * a))

entries.name: Physlib.RatComplexNum.toComplexNum_eq_add_neg_add_add_iff
entries.docstring:
Equality with a four-term sum of rational complex numbers can be checked before their
inclusion into the complex numbers.
entries.snippet:
lemma toComplexNum_eq_add_neg_add_add_iff {a b c d e : RatComplexNum} :
    (toComplexNum a = toComplexNum b + -toComplexNum c + toComplexNum d + toComplexNum e) ↔
      a = b + -c + d + e

entries.name: Real.completeEllipticK
entries.docstring:
The complete elliptic integral of the first kind in the parameter convention,
`K(m) = ∫ φ in 0..π/2, (1 - m sin² φ) ^ (-1/2)`. The physics literature often writes `K(k)`
with `m = k²`. The integrand is written as a real power rather than `1 / √(…)` so that
continuity, positivity and monotonicity in `m` come from the `rpow` API (`Continuous.rpow_const`,
`Real.rpow_pos_of_pos`, `Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_nonpos`); the two forms agree by
`Real.sqrt_eq_rpow` and `Real.rpow_neg`. For `m ≥ 1` see the module docstring.
entries.snippet:
@[pp_nodot]
noncomputable def completeEllipticK (m : ℝ) : ℝ

entries.name: Real.completeEllipticK_def
entries.docstring:
Unfolding lemma: `completeEllipticK m` is the interval integral of its integrand over
`[0, π/2]`.
entries.snippet:
lemma completeEllipticK_def (m : ℝ) :
    completeEllipticK m = ∫ φ in (0 : ℝ)..π / 2, (1 - m * sin φ ^ 2) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℝ))

entries.name: Real.completeEllipticK_radicand_pos
entries.docstring:
For `m < 1` the radicand `1 - m sin² φ` of the integrand of `completeEllipticK m` is
positive at every angle `φ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma completeEllipticK_radicand_pos {m : ℝ} (hm : m < 1) (φ : ℝ) :
    0 < 1 - m * sin φ ^ 2

entries.name: Real.continuous_completeEllipticK_integrand
entries.docstring:
For `m < 1` the integrand of `completeEllipticK m` is continuous, the real power being
taken at a positive base.
entries.snippet:
lemma continuous_completeEllipticK_integrand {m : ℝ} (hm : m < 1) :
    Continuous fun φ : ℝ => (1 - m * sin φ ^ 2) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℝ))

entries.name: Real.intervalIntegrable_completeEllipticK_integrand
entries.docstring: For `m < 1` the integrand of `completeEllipticK m` is interval integrable on `[0, π/2]`.
entries.snippet:
lemma intervalIntegrable_completeEllipticK_integrand {m : ℝ} (hm : m < 1) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun φ : ℝ => (1 - m * sin φ ^ 2) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℝ))) volume 0 (π / 2)

entries.name: Real.completeEllipticK_zero
entries.docstring: `K 0 = π / 2`: at parameter zero the integrand of `completeEllipticK` is the constant `1`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma completeEllipticK_zero : completeEllipticK 0 = π / 2

entries.name: Real.completeEllipticK_pos
entries.docstring: For `m < 1` the complete elliptic integral `completeEllipticK m` is positive.
entries.snippet: lemma completeEllipticK_pos {m : ℝ} (hm : m < 1) : 0 < completeEllipticK m

entries.name: Real.completeEllipticK_mono
entries.docstring:
`completeEllipticK` is monotone on its domain: for `m₁ ≤ m₂ < 1`, `K m₁ ≤ K m₂`. The
integrand is pointwise monotone in the parameter, the radicand being positive for both
parameters.
entries.snippet:
@[gcongr]
lemma completeEllipticK_mono {m₁ m₂ : ℝ} (h12 : m₁ ≤ m₂) (h2 : m₂ < 1) :
    completeEllipticK m₁ ≤ completeEllipticK m₂

entries.name: Real.monotoneOn_completeEllipticK
entries.docstring: `completeEllipticK` is monotone on its domain `(-∞, 1)`, as a `MonotoneOn` statement.
entries.snippet: lemma monotoneOn_completeEllipticK : MonotoneOn completeEllipticK (Set.Iio 1)

entries.name: Real.completeEllipticK_strictMono
entries.docstring:
`completeEllipticK` is strictly monotone on its domain: for `m₁ < m₂ < 1`, `K m₁ < K m₂`.
The pointwise inequality between the integrands is strict at `φ = π / 2`, where `sin² φ = 1`.
entries.snippet:
@[gcongr]
lemma completeEllipticK_strictMono {m₁ m₂ : ℝ} (h12 : m₁ < m₂) (h2 : m₂ < 1) :
    completeEllipticK m₁ < completeEllipticK m₂

entries.name: Real.strictMonoOn_completeEllipticK
entries.docstring: `completeEllipticK` is strictly increasing on `(-∞, 1)`, as a bundled `StrictMonoOn`.
entries.snippet: lemma strictMonoOn_completeEllipticK : StrictMonoOn completeEllipticK (Set.Iio 1)

entries.name: Real.pi_div_two_le_completeEllipticK
entries.docstring:
For `0 ≤ m < 1` the complete elliptic integral `completeEllipticK m` is at least its value
`π / 2` at `m = 0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma pi_div_two_le_completeEllipticK {m : ℝ} (hm0 : 0 ≤ m) (hm1 : m < 1) :
    π / 2 ≤ completeEllipticK m

entries.name: Real.completeEllipticK_le
entries.docstring:
For `0 ≤ m < 1` the complete elliptic integral `completeEllipticK m` is at most
`π / 2 * (1 - m) ^ (-1/2)`: the radicand is at least `1 - m`, `sin² φ` being at most `1`, so the
integrand is at most the constant `(1 - m) ^ (-1/2)`. With `pi_div_two_le_completeEllipticK` this
sandwiches `K` on `[0, 1)`; for the pendulum, where `m = sin² (θ₀ / 2)`, it bounds the period by
`T ≤ 2π √(ℓ / g) / cos (θ₀ / 2)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma completeEllipticK_le {m : ℝ} (hm0 : 0 ≤ m) (hm1 : m < 1) :
    completeEllipticK m ≤ π / 2 * (1 - m) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℝ))

entries.name: Real.continuousOn_completeEllipticK
entries.docstring: `completeEllipticK` is continuous on its domain `(-∞, 1)`.
entries.snippet: lemma continuousOn_completeEllipticK : ContinuousOn completeEllipticK (Set.Iio 1)

entries.name: Real.continuousAt_completeEllipticK
entries.docstring:
`completeEllipticK` is continuous at every point `m < 1` of its domain, `(-∞, 1)` being a
neighbourhood of `m`.
entries.snippet: lemma continuousAt_completeEllipticK {m : ℝ} (hm : m < 1) : ContinuousAt completeEllipticK m

entries.name: Real.continuousAt_completeEllipticK_zero
entries.docstring: `completeEllipticK` is continuous at `m = 0`, an interior point of its domain `(-∞, 1)`.
entries.snippet: lemma continuousAt_completeEllipticK_zero : ContinuousAt completeEllipticK 0

entries.name: Real.sin_sq_lt_one
entries.docstring: `sin x ^ 2 < 1` for `|x| < π / 2`: the cosine is positive there, and `1 - sin² x = cos² x`.
entries.snippet: lemma sin_sq_lt_one {x : ℝ} (h : |x| < π / 2) : sin x ^ 2 < 1

entries.name: Real.sin_half_sq_lt_one
entries.docstring:
The half-angle form of `sin_sq_lt_one`: `sin (θ / 2) ^ 2 < 1` for `|θ| < π`. For the pendulum
this says that the parameter `sin² (θ₀ / 2)` of the period formula lies in the domain of
`completeEllipticK` for every libration amplitude `|θ₀| < π`.
entries.snippet: lemma sin_half_sq_lt_one {θ : ℝ} (h : |θ| < π) : sin (θ / 2) ^ 2 < 1

The types of the declarations that `syntax`, `notation` and `macro` commands produce, along

Whether the final component of `declName` ends in an underscore followed by a number, the

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI
entries.docstring:
The representation of the gauge group `GaugeGroupI` on `HiggsVec`: the `SU(2)`
  factor acts by matrix multiplication, and the `U(1)` factor by scalar
  multiplication with its third power.
entries.snippet: def repGaugeGroupI : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI HiggsVec where

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_apply (g : StandardModel.GaugeGroupI) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    repGaugeGroupI g φ = (WithLp.toLp 2 <| g.toU1 ^ 3 • (g.toSU2.1 *ᵥ φ.ofLp))

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI_apply_eq_U1_mul_SU2
entries.snippet:

    repGaugeGroupI g φ = (WithLp.toLp 2 <| g.toSU2.1 *ᵥ (g.toU1 ^ 3 • φ.ofLp))

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI_apply_eq_U1_smul_SU2
entries.snippet:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_apply_eq_U1_smul_SU2 (g : StandardModel.GaugeGroupI) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    repGaugeGroupI g φ = (WithLp.toLp 2 <| (g.toU1 ^ 3 • g.toSU2.1) *ᵥ φ.ofLp)

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI_inner
entries.snippet:

lemma repGaugeGroupI_inner (g : StandardModel.GaugeGroupI) (φ ψ : HiggsVec) :
    ⟪repGaugeGroupI g φ, repGaugeGroupI g ψ⟫_ℂ = ⟪φ, ψ⟫_ℂ

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI_norm
entries.snippet:

lemma repGaugeGroupI_norm (g : StandardModel.GaugeGroupI) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    ‖repGaugeGroupI g φ‖ = ‖φ‖

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI_mul_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_mul_apply (g₁ g₂ : StandardModel.GaugeGroupI) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    repGaugeGroupI (g₁ * g₂) φ = repGaugeGroupI g₁ (repGaugeGroupI g₂ φ)

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI_inv_apply_eq_iff
entries.snippet:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_inv_apply_eq_iff (g : StandardModel.GaugeGroupI) (φ ψ : HiggsVec) :
    repGaugeGroupI g⁻¹ φ = ψ ↔ φ = repGaugeGroupI g ψ

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.toRealGroupElem_apply_self
entries.snippet:
lemma toRealGroupElem_apply_self (φ : HiggsVec) :
    repGaugeGroupI (toRealGroupElem φ) φ = ofReal (‖φ‖ ^ 2)

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.exists_repGaugeGroupI_eq_iff_norm_eq
entries.docstring:
Two Higgs vectors are in the same gauge orbit (i.e. related by `repGaugeGroupI`)
  if and only if they have the same norm.
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_repGaugeGroupI_eq_iff_norm_eq (φ : HiggsVec) (ψ : HiggsVec) :
    (∃ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g φ = ψ) ↔ ‖ψ‖ = ‖φ‖

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.ofU1Subgroup_repGaugeGroupI_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma ofU1Subgroup_repGaugeGroupI_apply (g : unitary ℂ) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    repGaugeGroupI (StandardModel.GaugeGroupI.ofU1Subgroup g) φ =
    (WithLp.toLp 2 <| !![1, 0; 0, g.1 ^ 6] *ᵥ φ.ofLp)

entries.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI_phase_snd
entries.snippet:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_phase_snd (φ : HiggsVec) :
    ∃ g : StandardModel.GaugeGroupI,
      (repGaugeGroupI g φ).ofLp 1 = ‖(φ.ofLp 1)‖ ∧
      (∀ φ1 : HiggsVec, (repGaugeGroupI g φ1).ofLp 0 = φ1.ofLp 0) ∧
      (∀ a : ℝ, repGaugeGroupI g (!₂[a, 0] : HiggsVec) = (!₂[a, 0] : HiggsVec))

entries.name: PureU1.Even.line_in_cubic_unshifted_unshifted_shifted
entries.docstring:
This lemma states that for a given `S` of type `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear` and
a proof `h` that the line through `S` lies on a cubic curve,
for any functions `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ` and `f : Fin n → ℚ`, if
`S.val = Unshifted.planeCharges g + Shifted.planeCharges f`,
then
`accCubeTriLinSymm.toFun (Unshifted.planeCharges g, Unshifted.planeCharges g,
  Shifted.planeCharges f) = 0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma line_in_cubic_unshifted_unshifted_shifted
    {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ)
      (_ : S.val = Unshifted.planeCharges g + Shifted.planeCharges f),
    accCubeTriLinSymm (Unshifted.planeCharges g) (Unshifted.planeCharges g)
      (Shifted.planeCharges f) = 0

entries.name: PureU1.Even.unshifted_unshifted_shifted_accCube'
entries.snippet:
lemma unshifted_unshifted_shifted_accCube' {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).LinSols}
    (f : Fin n.succ.succ → ℚ) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (hS : S.val = Pa f g) :
    accCubeTriLinSymm (Unshifted.planeCharges f) (Unshifted.planeCharges f)
      (Shifted.basisAsCharges (Fin.last n)) =
    - (S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))) *
    (2 * S.val evenShiftLast +
    S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n)))

entries.name: PureU1.VectorLikeOddPlane.Shifted.swap_as_add
entries.docstring:
Swapping the elements oddShiftFst j and oddShiftSnd j is equivalent to adding a vector
  basisAsCharges j.
entries.snippet:
lemma swap_as_add {S S' : (PureU1 (2 * n + 1)).LinSols} (j : Fin n)
    (hS : ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n + 1)).linSolRep
    (Equiv.swap (oddShiftFst j) (oddShiftSnd j))) S = S') :
    S'.val = S.val + (S.val (oddShiftSnd j) - S.val (oddShiftFst j)) • basisAsCharges j

entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ξEquiv_apply (x : Space d) (i : Fin d) : Q.ξEquiv x i = Q.ξ i * x i

entries.snippet:

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenEnergy
entries.docstring: The energy eigenvalues, `∑ i, ℏ ωᵢ (nᵢ + ½)`.
entries.snippet: def eigenEnergy : ℝ

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenEnergy_eq
entries.snippet: lemma eigenEnergy_eq : Q.eigenEnergy n = ∑ i, ℏ * Q.ω i * (n i + 1 / 2)

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenEnergy_strictMono
entries.snippet: lemma eigenEnergy_strictMono : StrictMono Q.eigenEnergy

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenCoeff
entries.docstring: The `i`th normalization constant for `Q.eigenfunction n`, `1 / √(2 ^ nᵢ * nᵢ! * √π * ξᵢ)`.
entries.snippet: def eigenCoeff (i : Fin d) : ℝ

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenCoeff_eq
entries.snippet: lemma eigenCoeff_eq (i : Fin d) : Q.eigenCoeff n i = 1 / √(2 ^ n i * (n i)! * √π * Q.ξ i)

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction
entries.docstring:
The eigenfunction labelled by the integer quantum numbers `n : Fin d → ℕ`, defined as a product
  of (physicist's) Hermite polynomials multiplying a Gaussian with covariance controlled
  by the characteristic lengths, `Q.ξ`.
entries.snippet: def eigenfunction : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma eigenfunction_eq :
    Q.eigenfunction n = compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv ℂ Q.ξEquiv.symm (smulLeftCLM ℂ
      (fun x ↦ ∏ i, Q.eigenCoeff n i * physHermite (n i) (x i)) (stdGaussian (Space d) ℂ))

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma eigenfunction_apply :
    Q.eigenfunction n x =
      ∏ i, Q.eigenCoeff n i *
        physHermite (n i) (x i / Q.ξ i) * cexp (-2⁻¹ * (x i / Q.ξ i) ^ 2)

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenstate

entries.snippet: def eigenstate : SchwartzSubmodule d

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenstate_eq
entries.snippet: lemma eigenstate_eq : Q.eigenstate n = schwartzEquiv _ (Q.eigenfunction n)

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenstates_orthonormal
entries.docstring: The energy eigenstates are orthonormal.
entries.snippet:
@[simp, sorryful]
lemma eigenstates_orthonormal : ⟪(Q.eigenstate n : Q.HS), Q.eigenstate n'⟫_ℂ = δ[n,n']

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.momentumState
entries.docstring:
Momentum state as a member of the strong dual of the Schwartz space.

  For a given `p` this corresponds to the non-normalizable plane wave `exp (I p ⬝ᵥ x)`.
entries.snippet: def momentumState (p : Space d) : StrongDual ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.momentumState_apply
entries.docstring: The defining property of momentum states.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma momentumState_apply (p : Space d) (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    momentumState p ψ = 𝓕 ψ ((2 * π)⁻¹ • p)

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.eq_of_eq_momentumState
entries.docstring: Two Schwartz maps are equal if they are equal on all momentum states.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_of_eq_momentumState {ψ φ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)}
    (h : ∀ p, momentumState p ψ = momentumState p φ) : ψ = φ

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.positionState
entries.docstring:
Position state as a member of the strong dual of the Schwartz space.

  For a given `x` this corresponds to the non-normalizable wavefunction `ψ(y) = δᵈ(y - x)
entries.snippet: def positionState (x : Space d) : StrongDual ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.positionState_apply
entries.docstring: The defining property of position states.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma positionState_apply (x : Space d) (f : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) : positionState x f = f x

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.eq_of_eq_positionState
entries.docstring: Two Schwartz maps are equal if they are equal on all position states.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_of_eq_positionState {f g : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)}
    (h : ∀ x, positionState x f = positionState x g) : f = g

entries.name: CompleteTensorProduct
entries.docstring:
The _completion_ of the tensor product of two inner product spaces `E` and `F` over `𝕜`.
  By construction this produces a Hilbert space. The localized notations are `E ⊗ₕ F`
  and `E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F`, accessed by `open scoped CompleteTensorProduct`.
entries.snippet:
def CompleteTensorProduct (𝕜 : Type*) [RCLike 𝕜]
    (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E]
    (F : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F] : Type _

entries.name: TensorProduct.instNontrivial

entries.snippet:
@[coe]
def coe' : E ⊗[𝕜] F → E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F

entries.docstring: Coercion from `E ⊗[𝕜] F` to its completion.
entries.snippet: instance : Coe (E ⊗[𝕜] F) (E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F)

entries.snippet: lemma denseRange_coe : DenseRange (coe' : E ⊗[𝕜] F → E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F)

@[norm_cast]
lemma coe_zero : (0 : E ⊗[𝕜] F) = (0 : E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F)

@[simp]

@[norm_cast]

entries.name: CompleteTensorProduct.coe_sub
entries.snippet:
@[norm_cast]
lemma coe_sub : (x - y : E ⊗[𝕜] F) = (x - y : E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F)

entries.snippet:
@[norm_cast]
lemma coe_add : (x + y : E ⊗[𝕜] F) = (x + y : E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F)

@[simp, norm_cast]
lemma coe_smul : (c • x : E ⊗[𝕜] F) = (c • x : E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F)

@[simp]
lemma norm_coe : ‖(x : E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F)‖ = ‖x‖

entries.name: CompleteTensorProduct.tInclₗᵢ

entries.name: CompleteTensorProduct.induction_on
entries.docstring:
An induction principle for `CompleteTensorProduct` combining those of `Completion`
  and `TensorProduct`.
entries.snippet:
@[elab_as_elim]
lemma induction_on {motive : E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F → Prop} (z : E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F)
    (zero : motive 0) (tmul : ∀ (x : E) (y : F), motive (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y))
    (add : ∀ x y : E ⊗[𝕜] F, motive x → motive y → motive ↑(x + y))
    (closed : IsClosed {x | motive x}) : motive z

entries.name: CompleteTensorProduct.comm
entries.docstring:
The complete tensor product of inner product spaces is commutative,
  up to linear isometric equivalence.
entries.snippet: def comm : E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] E

entries.name: CompleteTensorProduct.comm_symm
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma comm_symm : (comm 𝕜 E F).symm = comm 𝕜 F E

entries.name: CompleteTensorProduct.comm_coe
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma comm_coe (x : E ⊗[𝕜] F) : comm 𝕜 E F x = TensorProduct.comm 𝕜 E F x

entries.name: TensorProduct.denseRange_map
entries.docstring: The tensor product of a pair of linear maps with dense range also has dense range.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.TensorProduct.denseRange_map
    {R 𝕜 : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [RCLike 𝕜] {σ : R →+* 𝕜} [RingHomSurjective σ]
    {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] {N : Type*} [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N]
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E]
    {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F]
    {f : M →ₛₗ[σ] E} (hf : DenseRange f) {g : N →ₛₗ[σ] F} (hg : DenseRange g) :
    DenseRange (TensorProduct.map f g)

entries.name: CompleteTensorProduct.assoc
entries.docstring:
The compete tensor product of inner product spaces is associative,
  up to linear isometric equivalence.
entries.snippet: def assoc : E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] G ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] (F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] G)

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.angularMomentum_commutation_Ldot_p
entries.docstring:
A supporting piece of `angularMomentum_commutation_lrl`: how `𝐋ᵢⱼ` commutes with the
dot-product term `𝐋ₖ⬝ᵥ𝐩` appearing in `H.lrlOperator`'s expanded form (`lrlOperator_eq'`).
entries.snippet:
lemma angularMomentum_commutation_Ldot_p (i j k : Fin H.d) :
    ⁅𝐋[H.d] i j, 𝐋 k ⬝ᵥ 𝐩⁆ =
      (I * ℏ) • (δ[i,k] • (𝐋 j ⬝ᵥ 𝐩) - δ[j,k] • (𝐋 i ⬝ᵥ 𝐩))

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra
entries.docstring:
A unital complex C⋆-algebra with a compatible order making `≤` the usual positivity order.
Mathlib doesn't pick one canonically, so definitions below that need `≤` take this instead of
just `CStarAlgebra`.
entries.snippet: class OperatorAlgebra (A : Type*) extends CStarAlgebra A, PartialOrder A, StarOrderedRing A

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.Observable
entries.docstring:
An observable is a self-adjoint element of `A`: position, momentum, energy, spin, ... .
Self-adjointness is exactly what makes an element a *measurable* quantity — it is what forces its
spectrum, the possible measurement outcomes, to be real.
entries.snippet: noncomputable abbrev Observable (A : Type*) [OperatorAlgebra A]

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.PositiveElement
entries.docstring:
A positive element of `A`: an observable whose measurement outcomes are all `≥ 0`.
Positivity is what gives observables a meaningful order (`a ≤ b` meaning `b - a` is positive).
entries.snippet: abbrev PositiveElement (A : Type*) [OperatorAlgebra A]

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.Effect
entries.docstring:
An effect is an observable between zero and the identity, representing a yes/no measurement
outcome.
entries.snippet: abbrev Effect (A : Type*) [OperatorAlgebra A]

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.POVM
entries.docstring:
A finite POVM on `A`: the most general notion of a measurement with outcomes in `X`,
generalizing a single yes/no `Effect` to several possible outcomes.
entries.snippet:
structure POVM (A : Type*) [OperatorAlgebra A] (X : Type*) [Fintype X] where
  effect : X → Effect A
  sum_effect : ∑ x, (effect x : A) = 1

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.Unitary
entries.docstring:
A unitary element of `A`: implements a reversible transformation of the system — a symmetry,
or time evolution under a Hamiltonian — acting on observables by conjugation, `a ↦ U a U⋆`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable abbrev Unitary (A : Type*) [OperatorAlgebra A]

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.State
entries.docstring:
A state on `A`: a positive complex-linear functional normalized by `ω 1 = 1`. `ω a` is the
expected outcome of measuring observable `a` in this state — a state records everything that can
be learned about the system by measurement.
entries.snippet:
structure State (A : Type*) [OperatorAlgebra A] where
  toPositiveLinearMap : A →ₚ[ℂ] ℂ
  map_one : toPositiveLinearMap 1 = 1

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.Channel
entries.docstring:
A channel from `A₁` to `A₂` — physicists' name for a unital completely positive (UCP) map,
the most general notion of dynamics this framework expresses.
entries.snippet: abbrev Channel (A₁ A₂ : Type*) [OperatorAlgebra A₁] [OperatorAlgebra A₂]

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.conjStarAlgAut_surjective
entries.docstring: Every ⋆-automorphism of `B(H)` is implemented by unitary conjugation.
entries.snippet:
lemma conjStarAlgAut_surjective :
    Function.Surjective (Unitary.conjStarAlgAut ℂ (B(H)))

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.conjStarAlgAut_eq_iff
entries.docstring:
Two unitaries implement the same ⋆-automorphism of `B(H)` exactly when they differ by a scalar
phase.
entries.snippet:
lemma conjStarAlgAut_eq_iff (u v : Unitary (B(H))) :
    Unitary.conjStarAlgAut ℂ (B(H)) u =
        Unitary.conjStarAlgAut ℂ (B(H)) v ↔
      ∃ c : unitary ℂ, u = c • v

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.ProjectiveUnitary
entries.docstring: The projective unitary group of `H`, obtained by quotienting out scalar phases.
entries.snippet:
def ProjectiveUnitary (H : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
    [CompleteSpace H]

entries.snippet: noncomputable instance : Group (ProjectiveUnitary H)

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.projectiveUnitaryEquivStarAlgAut

entries.snippet:
noncomputable def projectiveUnitaryEquivStarAlgAut :
    ProjectiveUnitary H ≃* ((B(H)) ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] (B(H)))

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.Observable.jordan
entries.docstring: The symmetrized product of two observables.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def jordan (a b : Observable A) : Observable A

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.Observable.coe_jordan
entries.snippet:
lemma coe_jordan (a b : Observable A) :
    (a ⊙ b : A) = (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • ((a : A) * b + (b : A) * a)

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.Observable.jordan_comm
entries.snippet:
lemma jordan_comm (a b : Observable A) :
    a ⊙ b = b ⊙ a

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.Observable.jordan_self
entries.snippet:
lemma jordan_self (a : Observable A) :
    (a ⊙ a : A) = (a : A) * a

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.Observable.add_jordan
entries.snippet:
lemma add_jordan (a b c : Observable A) :
    (a + b) ⊙ c = a ⊙ c + b ⊙ c

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.Observable.jordan_add
entries.snippet:
lemma jordan_add (a b c : Observable A) :
    a ⊙ (b + c) = a ⊙ b + a ⊙ c

entries.name: OperatorAlgebra.Observable.jordan_smul
entries.snippet:
lemma jordan_smul (t : ℝ) (a b : Observable A) :
    a ⊙ (t • b) = t • (a ⊙ b)

entries.name: Lorentz.SL2C.boostAxis
entries.docstring:
The `SL(2,ℂ)` lift of the boost along spatial axis `i`, with `0 = x`, `1 = y`, and
`2 = z`. The parameter `t` is multiplicative, and for `t > 0` the rapidity is `2 * log t`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def boostAxis : Fin 3 → (t : ℝ) → t ≠ 0 → SL(2,ℂ)
  | 0, t, ht =>
      ⟨!![((t : ℂ) + (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2, ((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2;
          ((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2, ((t : ℂ) + (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2], by
        have htc : (t : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr ht
        rw [Matrix.det_fin_two_of]
        field_simp
        ring⟩
  | 1, t, ht =>
      ⟨!![((t : ℂ) + (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2, -Complex.I * ((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2;
          Complex.I * ((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2, ((t : ℂ) + (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2], by
        have htc : (t : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr ht
        have h2 : -Complex.I * ((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2 *
            (Complex.I * ((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2) =
            ((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2 * (((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2) := by
          have hI : -Complex.I * Complex.I = 1 := by
            rw [neg_mul, Complex.I_mul_I, neg_neg]
          calc -Complex.I * ((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2 *
                (Complex.I * ((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2)
              = (-Complex.I * Complex.I) *
                  (((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2 * (((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2)) := by
                ring
            _ = ((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2 * (((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2) := by
                rw [hI, one_mul]
        rw [Matrix.det_fin_two_of, h2]
        field_simp
        ring⟩
  | 2, t, ht =>
      ⟨!![(t : ℂ), 0; 0, (t : ℂ)⁻¹], by
        have htc : (t : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr ht
        rw [Matrix.det_fin_two_of]
        simp [mul_inv_cancel₀ htc]⟩

entries.name: Lorentz.SL2C.boostAxis_inv
entries.docstring: Inverting an axis boost replaces its multiplicative parameter `t` by `t⁻¹`.
entries.snippet:
lemma boostAxis_inv (i : Fin 3) (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    (boostAxis i t ht)⁻¹ = boostAxis i t⁻¹ (inv_ne_zero ht)

entries.name: Lorentz.SL2C.boostAxis_conjTranspose
entries.docstring: The matrix underlying an axis-boost lift is Hermitian.
entries.snippet:
lemma boostAxis_conjTranspose (i : Fin 3) (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    (boostAxis i t ht).1ᴴ = (boostAxis i t ht).1

entries.name: Lorentz.SL2C.boostAxis_eq_conj
entries.docstring: Every axis boost is obtained by conjugating the `z`-axis boost by `rotationZToAxis`.
entries.snippet:
lemma boostAxis_eq_conj (i : Fin 3) (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    boostAxis i t ht =
      rotationZToAxis i * boostAxis 2 t ht * (rotationZToAxis i)⁻¹

entries.name: Lorentz.SL2C.exists_conj_boostAxis
entries.docstring: Every coordinate-axis boost is conjugate to the `z`-axis boost.
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_conj_boostAxis (i : Fin 3) :
    ∃ R : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0),
      boostAxis i t ht = R * boostAxis 2 t ht * R⁻¹

entries.name: LorentzGroup.boostAxis
entries.docstring:
The Lorentz transformation induced by the multiplicatively parameterized `SL(2,ℂ)` boost
along spatial axis `i`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def boostAxis (i : Fin 3) (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) : LorentzGroup 3

entries.name: LorentzGroup.boostAxis_apply
entries.docstring: The entries of an axis boost in the Lorentz group.
entries.snippet:
lemma boostAxis_apply (i : Fin 3) (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) (a b : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (boostAxis i t ht).1 a b =
      if a = Sum.inl 0 ∧ b = Sum.inl 0 then (t ^ 2 + (t⁻¹) ^ 2) / 2
      else if a = Sum.inl 0 ∧ b = Sum.inr i then -((t ^ 2 - (t⁻¹) ^ 2) / 2)
      else if a = Sum.inr i ∧ b = Sum.inl 0 then -((t ^ 2 - (t⁻¹) ^ 2) / 2)
      else if a = Sum.inr i ∧ b = Sum.inr i then (t ^ 2 + (t⁻¹) ^ 2) / 2
      else if a = b then 1 else 0

entries.name: minkowskiMatrix.vecMul_apply
entries.docstring:
Right multiplication of a row vector by the Minkowski matrix multiplies each component by
the corresponding diagonal sign.
entries.snippet:
lemma vecMul_apply (v : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) → ℝ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    (v ᵥ* minkowskiMatrix) μ = v μ * minkowskiMatrix μ μ

entries.name: minkowskiMatrix.prod_diagonal
entries.docstring: The product of all diagonal entries of the Minkowski matrix is `(-1) ^ d`.
entries.snippet: lemma prod_diagonal : ∏ μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d, minkowskiMatrix μ μ = (-1) ^ d

entries.name: minkowskiMatrix.prod_diagonal_comp_of_injective
entries.docstring: Reindexing all diagonal entries injectively does not change their product.

entries.name: PauliMatrix.pauliMatrix_anticommutator
entries.docstring: Pauli matrices satisfy `{σᵢ, σⱼ} = 2 δᵢⱼ I`.
entries.snippet:
lemma pauliMatrix_anticommutator (i j : Fin 3) :
    pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i) * pauliMatrix (Sum.inr j) +
      pauliMatrix (Sum.inr j) * pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i) =
        ((2 * kroneckerDelta i j : ℕ) : ℂ) •
          (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)

entries.name: PauliMatrix.vectorMatrix
entries.docstring: The matrix `a · σ` associated to a real three-vector `a`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def vectorMatrix (a : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ

entries.name: PauliMatrix.vectorMatrix_anticommutator
entries.docstring:
The anticommutator of two Pauli vectors is twice their Euclidean dot product
times the identity.
entries.snippet:
lemma vectorMatrix_anticommutator (a b : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    vectorMatrix a * vectorMatrix b + vectorMatrix b * vectorMatrix a =
      ((2 * (a ⬝ᵥ b) : ℝ) : ℂ) •
        (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)

entries.name: PauliMatrix.vectorMatrix_commutator
entries.docstring:
The commutator of two Pauli vectors is twice `i` times the Pauli vector
associated to their cross product.
entries.snippet:
lemma vectorMatrix_commutator (a b : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    vectorMatrix a * vectorMatrix b - vectorMatrix b * vectorMatrix a =
      (2 * Complex.I) • vectorMatrix (a ⨯₃ b)

entries.name: PauliMatrix.vectorMatrix_mul_vectorMatrix
entries.docstring:
Product formula for Pauli vectors:
`(a · σ)(b · σ) = (a · b) I + i (a × b) · σ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma vectorMatrix_mul_vectorMatrix (a b : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    vectorMatrix a * vectorMatrix b =
      ((a ⬝ᵥ b : ℝ) : ℂ) •
          (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) +
        Complex.I • vectorMatrix (a ⨯₃ b)

entries.name: PauliMatrix.vectorMatrix_sq
entries.docstring: The square of `a · σ` is `|a|² I`.
entries.snippet:
lemma vectorMatrix_sq (a : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    vectorMatrix a * vectorMatrix a =
      (∑ i : Fin 3, a i ^ 2 : ℝ) • 1

entries.name: PauliMatrix.pauliContr_mul_dualWeyl_eq_ofRat
entries.docstring:
Rational-complex components of a contraction of `σ^^^` with a copy whose Weyl indices
are dualized.
entries.snippet:
lemma pauliContr_mul_dualWeyl_eq_ofRat :
    {σ^^^ | μ α β ⊗ σ^^^ | ν τ(α') τ(β)}ᵀ = ofRat (fun b =>
      ∑ x : Fin 2, pauliContrComponent (b 0) (b 1) x *
        pauliContrDownComponent (b 2) x (b 3))

entries.name: PauliMatrix.dualWeyl_mul_pauliContr_eq_ofRat
entries.docstring:
Rational-complex components of the reverse contraction of a Weyl-dualized `σ^^^` with
`σ^^^`.
entries.snippet:
lemma dualWeyl_mul_pauliContr_eq_ofRat :
    {σ^^^ | μ τ(α) τ(β) ⊗ σ^^^ | ν α β'}ᵀ = ofRat (fun b =>
      ∑ x : Fin 2, pauliContrDownComponent (b 0) (b 1) x *
        pauliContrComponent (b 2) x (b 3))

entries.name: PauliMatrix.leviCivita_mul_pauliDual
entries.docstring:
Contracting `ε4ℂ` with a Lorentz-dualized `σ^^^` agrees with contracting it with
`pauliCo`.
entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivita_mul_pauliDual :
    ({ε4ℂ | μ ν ρ κ ⊗ σ^^^ | τ(κ) α β =
      ε4ℂ | μ ν ρ κ ⊗ σ_^^ | κ α β}ᵀ : Prop)

entries.name: PauliMatrix.pauliContr_mul_pauliContrDown_mul_pauliContr
entries.docstring:
Equation (2.26), the three-Pauli identity
`σ^μ barσ^ν σ^ρ = g^{μν} σ^ρ - g^{μρ} σ^ν + g^{νρ} σ^μ
  + i ε^{μνρκ} σ_κ`, with barred and lowered forms expressed through index dualization `τ`.

entries.name: PauliMatrix.pauliContrDown_mul_pauliContr_mul_pauliContrDown
entries.docstring:
Equation (2.27), the conjugate three-Pauli identity
`barσ^μ σ^ν barσ^ρ = g^{μν} barσ^ρ - g^{μρ} barσ^ν + g^{νρ} barσ^μ
  - i ε^{μνρκ} barσ_κ`, with barred and lowered forms expressed through index dualization `τ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma pauliContrDown_mul_pauliContr_mul_pauliContrDown : ({
    σ^^^ | μ τ(α) τ(β) ⊗ σ^^^ | ν α β' ⊗ σ^^^ | ρ τ(α') τ(β') =
      ((((η | μ ν ⊗ σ^^^ | ρ τ(α') τ(β))
        + (-((η | μ ρ ⊗ σ^^^ | ν τ(α') τ(β)))))
        + (η | ν ρ ⊗ σ^^^ | μ τ(α') τ(β)))
        + ((-Complex.I) •ₜ (ε4ℂ | μ ν ρ κ ⊗ σ^^^ | τ(κ) τ(α') τ(β))))
    }ᵀ : Prop)

entries.name: PauliMatrix.trace_pauliMatrix_mul_pauliMatrix
entries.docstring: Pauli matrices are orthogonal with respect to the trace pairing: `tr(σ_μ σ_ν) = 2 δ_μν`.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma trace_pauliMatrix_mul_pauliMatrix (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    Matrix.trace (pauliMatrix μ * pauliMatrix ν) = ((2 * kroneckerDelta μ ν : ℕ) : ℂ)

entries.name: PauliMatrix.pauliCoeff
entries.docstring: The four real Pauli coefficients of a self-adjoint `2 × 2` matrix.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def pauliCoeff
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → ℝ
  | Sum.inl 0 => 1 / 2 * (Matrix.trace (σ0 * A.1)).re
  | Sum.inr 0 => 1 / 2 * (Matrix.trace (σ1 * A.1)).re
  | Sum.inr 1 => 1 / 2 * (Matrix.trace (σ2 * A.1)).re
  | Sum.inr 2 => 1 / 2 * (Matrix.trace (σ3 * A.1)).re

entries.name: PauliMatrix.sum_pauliCoeff
entries.docstring: Every self-adjoint `2 × 2` matrix is its Pauli decomposition.
entries.snippet:
lemma sum_pauliCoeff
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    ∑ i, pauliCoeff A i • pauliSelfAdjoint i = A

entries.name: PauliMatrix.eq_sum_pauli
entries.docstring: Every self-adjoint `2 × 2` matrix is a real linear combination of the Pauli matrices.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_sum_pauli
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    A = ∑ i, pauliCoeff A i • pauliSelfAdjoint i

entries.name: PauliMatrix.scalarCoeff
entries.docstring: The coefficient of the identity in the Pauli decomposition.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def scalarCoeff
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) : ℝ

entries.name: PauliMatrix.vectorCoeff
entries.docstring: The three spatial Pauli coefficients.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def vectorCoeff
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) : Fin 3 → ℝ

entries.name: PauliMatrix.vectorPart
entries.docstring: The traceless Pauli-vector part `a · σ`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def vectorPart
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ

entries.name: PauliMatrix.pauliRadius
entries.docstring: The Euclidean length of the spatial Pauli coefficients.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def pauliRadius
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) : ℝ

entries.name: PauliMatrix.pauliRadius_sq
entries.docstring:
The Pauli radius is the square root of the squared Euclidean length of the
spatial Pauli coefficients.
entries.snippet:
lemma pauliRadius_sq
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    pauliRadius A ^ 2 =
      ∑ i : Fin 3, vectorCoeff A i ^ 2

entries.name: PauliMatrix.pauliRadius_nonneg
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma pauliRadius_nonneg
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    0 ≤ pauliRadius A

entries.name: PauliMatrix.matrix_eq_scalar_add_vector
entries.docstring: A self-adjoint matrix is its scalar part plus its Pauli-vector part.
entries.snippet:
lemma matrix_eq_scalar_add_vector
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    A.val = (scalarCoeff A : ℂ) • 1 + vectorPart A

entries.name: PauliMatrix.trace_eq_two_mul_scalarCoeff
entries.docstring: The trace of a self-adjoint matrix is twice its scalar Pauli coefficient.
entries.snippet:
lemma trace_eq_two_mul_scalarCoeff
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    Matrix.trace A.1 = 2 * scalarCoeff A

entries.name: PauliMatrix.trace_vectorPart
entries.docstring: The Pauli-vector part has zero trace.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma trace_vectorPart
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    Matrix.trace (vectorPart A) = 0

entries.name: PauliMatrix.vectorPart_sq
entries.docstring:
The square of the vector part of a self-adjoint matrix is its squared
Pauli radius times the identity.
entries.snippet:
lemma vectorPart_sq
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    vectorPart A * vectorPart A =
      (pauliRadius A ^ 2 : ℝ) • 1

entries.name: PauliMatrix.trace_pauliSelfAdjoint'_mul
entries.docstring:
Trace orthogonality of the covariant Pauli basis:
  `tr (σ'_a σ'_b) = 2 δ_{a b}`.
entries.snippet:
lemma trace_pauliSelfAdjoint'_mul (a b : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    Matrix.trace ((pauliSelfAdjoint' a).1 * (pauliSelfAdjoint' b).1) =
      if a = b then 2 else 0

entries.name: PauliMatrix.trace_pauliSelfAdjoint'_mul_apply
entries.docstring:
The trace pairing of a covariant Pauli matrix with an arbitrary matrix, expressed through the
matrix entries.
entries.snippet:
lemma trace_pauliSelfAdjoint'_mul_apply (l : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (N : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    Matrix.trace ((pauliSelfAdjoint' l).1 * N) =
      match l with
      | Sum.inl 0 => N 0 0 + N 1 1
      | Sum.inr 0 => -(N 0 1 + N 1 0)
      | Sum.inr 1 => -(Complex.I * (N 0 1 - N 1 0))
      | Sum.inr 2 => -(N 0 0 - N 1 1)

entries.name: PauliMatrix.pauliContrComponent
entries.docstring: Rational-complex components of the contravariant Pauli four-vector.
entries.snippet: def pauliContrComponent (mu : Fin 4) (a b : Fin 2) : Physlib.RatComplexNum

entries.name: PauliMatrix.pauliContrDownComponent
entries.docstring: Rational-complex components of the contravariant conjugate Pauli four-vector.
entries.snippet: def pauliContrDownComponent (mu : Fin 4) (a b : Fin 2) : Physlib.RatComplexNum

entries.name: PauliMatrix.toTensor_dualLeft_eq_ofRat
entries.docstring: Rational-complex components of `σ^^^` after dualizing its left-handed Weyl index.
entries.snippet:
lemma toTensor_dualLeft_eq_ofRat :
    {σ^^^ | μ τ(α) β}ᵀ =
      ofRat (fun b =>
        ∑ x : Fin 2, pauliContrComponent (b 0) x (b 2) *
          (if x.val = 0 ∧ (b 1).val = 1 then 1 else
            if (b 1).val = 0 ∧ x.val = 1 then -1 else 0))

entries.name: PauliMatrix.toTensor_dualWeyl_eq_ofRat
entries.docstring: Rational-complex components of `σ^^^` after dualizing both Weyl indices.
entries.snippet:
lemma toTensor_dualWeyl_eq_ofRat :
    {σ^^^ | μ τ(α) τ(β)}ᵀ =
      ofRat (fun b =>
        pauliContrDownComponent (b 0) (b 2) (b 1))

entries.name: PauliMatrix.toTensor_dualLorentz_eq_ofRat
entries.docstring: Rational-complex components of `σ^^^` after dualizing its Lorentz index.
entries.snippet:
lemma toTensor_dualLorentz_eq_ofRat :
    {σ^^^ | τ(μ) α β}ᵀ =
      ofRat (fun b => pauliContrDownComponent (b 0) (b 1) (b 2))

entries.name: PauliMatrix.toTensor_dualLorentzLeft_eq_ofRat
entries.docstring:
Rational-complex components of `σ^^^` after dualizing its Lorentz and left-handed Weyl
indices.
entries.snippet:
lemma toTensor_dualLorentzLeft_eq_ofRat :
    {σ^^^ | τ(μ) τ(α) β}ᵀ = ofRat (fun b =>
      ∑ x : Fin 2, pauliContrDownComponent (b 0) x (b 2) *
        (if x.val = 0 ∧ (b 1).val = 1 then 1 else
          if (b 1).val = 0 ∧ x.val = 1 then -1 else 0))

entries.name: PauliMatrix.toTensor_dualAll_eq_ofRat
entries.docstring: Rational-complex components of `σ^^^` after dualizing all three indices.
entries.snippet:
lemma toTensor_dualAll_eq_ofRat :
    {σ^^^ | τ(μ) τ(α) τ(β)}ᵀ =
      ofRat (fun b => pauliContrComponent (b 0) (b 2) (b 1))

entries.name: PauliMatrix.toTensor_dualWeyl_eq_pauliContrDown
entries.docstring: Dualizing both Weyl indices of `σ^^^` gives `σ^__`.
entries.snippet:
lemma toTensor_dualWeyl_eq_pauliContrDown :
    ({σ^^^ | μ τ(α) τ(β) = σ^__ | μ β α}ᵀ : Prop)

entries.name: PauliMatrix.toTensor_dualAll_eq_pauliCoDown
entries.docstring: Dualizing all three indices of `σ^^^` gives `σ___`.
entries.snippet:
lemma toTensor_dualAll_eq_pauliCoDown :
    ({σ^^^ | τ(μ) τ(α) τ(β) = σ___ | μ β α}ᵀ : Prop)

entries.name: PauliMatrix.pauliDual_eq_pauliCo
entries.docstring: Lowering the Lorentz index of `σ^^^` with `τ` gives `σ_^^`.
entries.snippet:
lemma pauliDual_eq_pauliCo :
    ({σ^^^ | τ(μ) α β = σ_^^ | μ α β}ᵀ : Prop)

entries.name: PauliMatrix.pauliContrDownDual_eq_pauliCoDown
entries.docstring: Lowering the Lorentz index of `σ^__` with `τ` gives `σ___`.
entries.snippet:
lemma pauliContrDownDual_eq_pauliCoDown :
    ({σ^__ | τ(μ) β α = σ___ | μ β α}ᵀ : Prop)

entries.name: Lorentz.SL2C.rotationZToAxis
entries.docstring: The `SL(2,ℂ)` rotation carrying the `z`-axis to axis `i`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def rotationZToAxis : Fin 3 → SL(2,ℂ)
  | 0 =>
      ⟨(((Real.sqrt 2 : ℝ) : ℂ))⁻¹ • !![1, -1; 1, 1], by
        rw [Matrix.det_smul, Matrix.det_fin_two_of, Fintype.card_fin, inv_pow]
        norm_num [← Complex.ofReal_pow, Real.sq_sqrt]⟩
  | 1 =>
      ⟨(((Real.sqrt 2 : ℝ) : ℂ))⁻¹ • !![1, Complex.I; Complex.I, 1], by
        rw [Matrix.det_smul, Matrix.det_fin_two_of, Fintype.card_fin, inv_pow,
          Complex.I_mul_I]
        norm_num [← Complex.ofReal_pow, Real.sq_sqrt]⟩
  | 2 => 1

entries.name: Lorentz.SL2C.rotationZToAxis_zero_mul_diagonal_mul_inv
entries.docstring:
Conjugating `diag(a, b)` by the rotation to the `x`-axis expresses it in the `x`-axis
basis.
entries.snippet:
lemma rotationZToAxis_zero_mul_diagonal_mul_inv (a b : ℂ) :
    (rotationZToAxis 0).1 * !![a, 0; 0, b] * ((rotationZToAxis 0)⁻¹).1 =
      !![(a + b) / 2, (a - b) / 2; (a - b) / 2, (a + b) / 2]

entries.name: Lorentz.SL2C.rotationZToAxis_one_mul_diagonal_mul_inv
entries.docstring:
Conjugating `diag(a, b)` by the rotation to the `y`-axis expresses it in the `y`-axis
basis.
entries.snippet:
lemma rotationZToAxis_one_mul_diagonal_mul_inv (a b : ℂ) :
    (rotationZToAxis 1).1 * !![a, 0; 0, b] * ((rotationZToAxis 1)⁻¹).1 =
      !![(a + b) / 2, -Complex.I * (a - b) / 2;
        Complex.I * (a - b) / 2, (a + b) / 2]

entries.name: Lorentz.SL2C.rotationZToAxis_two_mul_diagonal_mul_inv
entries.docstring: Conjugating `diag(a, b)` by the identity rotation leaves it unchanged.
entries.snippet:
lemma rotationZToAxis_two_mul_diagonal_mul_inv (a b : ℂ) :
    (rotationZToAxis 2).1 * !![a, 0; 0, b] * ((rotationZToAxis 2)⁻¹).1 =
      !![a, 0; 0, b]

entries.name: Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup_eq_trace
entries.docstring:
The matrix elements of the covering map through the trace pairing:
  `L(M)_{i j} = ½ tr (σ'_i · M σ'_j M†)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma toLorentzGroup_eq_trace (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (i j : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (((toLorentzGroup M).1 i j : ℝ) : ℂ) =
      Matrix.trace ((PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint' i).1 *
        (M.1 * (PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint' j).1 * M.1ᴴ)) / 2

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.ComponentIdx.DropPairSection.ofFinEquiv_dropPair
entries.docstring: Restoring the two entries dropped from a component index recovers that component index.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ofFinEquiv_dropPair {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1 + 1) → C}
    {i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)} (hij : i ≠ j) (r : ComponentIdx (S := S) c) :
    (ofFinEquiv (S := S) hij (r.dropPair i j) (r i, r j)).1 = r

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.crossToSlot_basis_repr_apply
entries.docstring:
A component of `crossToSlot` is the corresponding component of `crossToEnd`, with the
surviving indices rotated back into the contracted slot.
entries.snippet:
lemma crossToSlot_basis_repr_apply {nA : ℕ} {c : Fin (nA + 1) → C} {cM : Fin 2 → C}
    (i : Fin (nA + 1)) (j : Fin 2) (hc : S.τ (c i) = cM j) (M : Tensor S cM)
    (t : Tensor S c)
    (φ : ComponentIdx (S := S) (Function.update c i (cM (j.succAbove 0)))) :
    (basis _).repr (crossToSlot i j hc M t) φ =
      (basis _).repr (crossToEnd i j hc t M) (fun m =>
        basisIdxCongr ((IsReindexing.crossToSlot_cycle i j).inv_perserve_color m)
          (φ ((IsReindexing.crossToSlot_cycle i j).inv
            ⇑(Fin.cycleIcc i (Fin.last nA)).symm m)))

entries.name: Fin.succSuccAbove_succAbove_comm_apply
entries.docstring: Pointwise form of commuting deletion of one slot with deletion of a pair.
entries.snippet:
lemma succSuccAbove_succAbove_comm_apply {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1 + 1))
    (k : Fin (n + 1)) (m : Fin n) :
    (i.succSuccAbove j k).succAbove
        (((Fin.predAbove 0 (i.succSuccAbove j k)).predAbove i).succSuccAbove
          ((Fin.predAbove 0 (i.succSuccAbove j k)).predAbove j) m) =
      i.succSuccAbove j (k.succAbove m)

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.evalT_evalT_basis
entries.docstring: Commutation of two evaluations on a tensor basis vector.
entries.snippet:
lemma evalT_evalT_basis {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1 + 1) → C}
    (k1 : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (k2 : Fin (n + 1)) (φ1 : basisIdx (c k1))
    (φ2 : basisIdx ((c ∘ k1.succAbove) k2)) (ψ : ComponentIdx (S := S) c) :
    evalT k2 φ2 (evalT k1 φ1 (basis (S := S) c ψ)) =
      permT id (IsReindexing.succAbove_succAbove_comm k1 k2)
        (evalT (k2.predAbove k1)
          (basisIdxCongr
            (congrArg c (Fin.succAbove_succAbove_predAbove k1 k2).symm) φ1)
          (evalT (k1.succAbove k2) φ2 (basis (S := S) c ψ)))

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.evalT_evalT
entries.docstring:
Evaluating two tensor indices commutes, up to the canonical reindexing
identifying the two possible orders in which the indices are removed.
entries.snippet:
lemma evalT_evalT {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1 + 1) → C}
    (k1 : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (k2 : Fin (n + 1)) (φ1 : basisIdx (c k1))
    (φ2 : basisIdx ((c ∘ k1.succAbove) k2)) (t : Tensor S c) :
    evalT k2 φ2 (evalT k1 φ1 t) =
      permT id (IsReindexing.succAbove_succAbove_comm k1 k2)
        (evalT (k2.predAbove k1)
          (basisIdxCongr
            (congrArg c (Fin.succAbove_succAbove_predAbove k1 k2).symm) φ1)
          (evalT (k1.succAbove k2) φ2 t))

entries.name: euclidLeviCivita_eq_leviCivitaSymbol
entries.docstring:
The Euclidean Levi-Civita symbol in dimension 4 is the general-dimension
Levi-Civita symbol `leviCivitaSymbol` at `ι = Fin 4`, carried to the reals.
entries.snippet:
lemma _root_.euclidLeviCivita_eq_leviCivitaSymbol (g : Fin 4 → Fin 4) :
    euclidLeviCivita g = (leviCivitaSymbol g : ℝ)

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.leviCivita_basis_repr_eq_leviCivitaSymbol
entries.docstring:
The components of the Levi-Civita tensor in the standard basis are the
general-dimension Levi-Civita symbol `leviCivitaSymbol` of the multi-index at
`ι = Fin 4`.
entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivita_basis_repr_eq_leviCivitaSymbol
    (b : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor 3) ![Color.up, Color.up, Color.up, Color.up]) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr ε4 b
      = (leviCivitaSymbol (fun i => finSumFinEquiv (b i)) : ℝ)

entries.name: complexLorentzTensor.leviCivita_isReindexing
entries.docstring:
The index colors of the complexified real Levi-Civita tensor agree with four complex
contravariant Lorentz indices.
entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivita_isReindexing : IsReindexing
    (realLorentzTensor.colorToComplex ∘
      ![realLorentzTensor.Color.up, realLorentzTensor.Color.up,
        realLorentzTensor.Color.up, realLorentzTensor.Color.up])
    ![Color.up, Color.up, Color.up, Color.up] id

entries.name: complexLorentzTensor.basisIdxCongr_val
entries.docstring: A color cast in the complex Lorentz basis preserves the underlying finite index value.
entries.snippet:
private lemma basisIdxCongr_val {c c1 : Color} (h : c = c1)
    (i : Fin (complexLorentzTensor.repDim c)) :
    (TensorSpecies.basisIdxCongr
      (basisIdx := fun c => Fin (complexLorentzTensor.repDim c)) h i).val = i.val

entries.name: complexLorentzTensor.leviCivita
entries.docstring: The Levi-Civita tensor `εᵘᵛᵖᵟ` as a complex Lorentz tensor, with `ε⁰¹²³ = 1`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def leviCivita : ℂT[.up, .up, .up, .up]

entries.name: complexLorentzTensor.leviCivita_eq_ofRat
entries.docstring:
The complex Levi-Civita tensor has the Levi-Civita symbol as its real component and zero
imaginary component in the standard basis.
entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivita_eq_ofRat : ε4ℂ = ofRat (fun
    b : ComponentIdx (S := complexLorentzTensor) ![Color.up, Color.up, Color.up, Color.up] =>
    ⟨generalizedKroneckerDelta
      (fun i => Fin.cast (by fin_cases i <;> rfl) (b i)) (id : Fin 4 → Fin 4), 0⟩)

entries.name: euclidLeviCivita_symbol_contract_one_last
entries.docstring:
**Triple Euclidean Levi-Civita contraction with the free index last.** This is the same
contraction as `euclidLeviCivita_symbol_contract_one`, in the slot order produced by the tensor
notation for `ε^{μνρσ} ε_{μνρτ}`.
entries.snippet:
lemma euclidLeviCivita_symbol_contract_one_last (a b : Fin 4) :
    ∑ h : Fin 3 → Fin 4, euclidLeviCivita (Fin.snoc h a) * euclidLeviCivita (Fin.snoc h b)
      = 6 * ((kroneckerDelta a b : ℕ) : ℝ)

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.leviCivita_lowered_basis_repr_apply
entries.docstring:
Lowering all four indices of the Levi-Civita tensor changes the sign of every standard-basis
component. This is the tensor-component form of the Lorentzian orientation factor
`det η = -1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivita_lowered_basis_repr_apply
    (b : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor 3)
      ![Color.down, Color.down, Color.down, Color.down]) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr ({ε4 | τ(μ) τ(ν) τ(ρ) τ(σ)}ᵀ) b =
      - (Tensor.basis _).repr ε4 b

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.leviCivita_basis_contract_self
entries.docstring:
The sum of the squared standard-basis components of the contravariant Levi-Civita tensor is
`4! = 24`.
entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivita_basis_contract_self :
    ∑ b : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor 3)
        ![Color.up, Color.up, Color.up, Color.up],
      (Tensor.basis _).repr ε4 b * (Tensor.basis _).repr ε4 b = 24

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.leviCivita_basis_contract_three
entries.docstring:
Contracting the first three standard-basis components of two contravariant Levi-Civita tensors
gives `3! = 6` times the Kronecker delta on the remaining components.
entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivita_basis_contract_three (a b : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ∑ h : Fin 3 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3,
      (Tensor.basis _).repr ε4 (Fin.snoc h a) *
      (Tensor.basis _).repr ε4 (Fin.snoc h b) =
      6 * (if a = b then 1 else 0)

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.leviCivita_contract_three_basis_repr_apply
entries.docstring:
The standard-basis component formula for the tensor contraction
`ε^{μνρσ} ε_{μνρτ}`.
entries.snippet:
lemma leviCivita_contract_three_basis_repr_apply
    (b : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor 3) ![Color.up, Color.down]) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr
        {ε4 | μ ν ρ σ ⊗ ε4 | τ(μ) τ(ν) τ(ρ) τ(τ)}ᵀ b =
      ∑ h : Fin 3 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3,
        (Tensor.basis _).repr ε4 (Fin.snoc h (b 0)) *
          (Tensor.basis _).repr ({ε4 | τ(μ) τ(ν) τ(ρ) τ(σ)}ᵀ) (Fin.snoc h (b 1))

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.leviCivita_contract_self_eq_sum
entries.docstring:
Fully contracting the tensor product of `ε4` and its fully lowered form is the sum of the
products of their matching standard-basis components.
entries.snippet:
@[nolint checkType]
lemma leviCivita_contract_self_eq_sum :
    {ε4 | μ ν ρ σ ⊗ ε4 | τ(μ) τ(ν) τ(ρ) τ(σ)}ᵀ.toField =
      ∑ b : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor 3)
          ![Color.up, Color.up, Color.up, Color.up],
        (Tensor.basis _).repr ε4 b *
          (Tensor.basis _).repr ({ε4 | τ(μ) τ(ν) τ(ρ) τ(σ)}ᵀ) b

entries.name: TensorSpecies.metricTensor_basis_repr
entries.docstring:
A component of the metric tensor is the corresponding component of the metric intertwiner
in the tensor-product basis.
entries.snippet:
lemma metricTensor_basis_repr (c : C) (φ : ComponentIdx (S := S) ![c, c]) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (metricTensor (S := S) c) φ =
      (Module.Basis.tensorProduct (b c) (b c)).repr ((S.metric c) (1 : k)) (φ 0, φ 1)

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.crossToEnd_basis_repr_apply_eq_fin
entries.docstring:
For real Lorentz tensors, the component formula for `crossToEnd` collapses to one sum because
the standard contravariant and covariant bases are dual under contraction.
entries.snippet:
lemma crossToEnd_basis_repr_apply_eq_fin {d nA nB : ℕ} {cA : Fin (nA + 1) → Color}
    {cB : Fin (nB + 1) → Color} (i : Fin (nA + 1)) (j : Fin (nB + 1))
    (hc : (realLorentzTensor d).τ (cA i) = cB j) (t : ℝT(d, cA)) (M : ℝT(d, cB))
    (φ : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor d)
      (Fin.append (cA ∘ i.succAbove) (cB ∘ j.succAbove))) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (crossToEnd i j hc t M) φ =
      ∑ x : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d,
        (Tensor.basis cA).repr t (i.insertNth x (fun m => φ (Fin.castAdd nB m))) *
          (Tensor.basis cB).repr M (j.insertNth x (fun m => φ (Fin.natAdd nA m)))

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.metricTensor_repr_apply_eq_minkowskiMatrix
entries.docstring: The component matrix of either real Lorentz metric tensor is the Minkowski matrix.
entries.snippet:
lemma metricTensor_repr_apply_eq_minkowskiMatrix {d : ℕ} (c : Color)
    (φ : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor d) ![c, c]) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (metricTensor (S := realLorentzTensor d) c) φ =
      minkowskiMatrix (φ 0) (φ 1)

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.toDualMapAtIndex_basis_repr_apply
entries.docstring:
Raising or lowering one index of a real Lorentz tensor contracts that slot's components with
the Minkowski matrix.
entries.snippet:
lemma toDualMapAtIndex_basis_repr_apply {d n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → Color}
    (i : Fin (n + 1)) (t : ℝT(d, c))
    (φ : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor d)
      (Function.update c i ((realLorentzTensor d).τ (c i)))) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (Tensor.toDualMapAtIndex (S := realLorentzTensor d) i t) φ =
      ∑ x : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d,
        (Tensor.basis c).repr t (i.insertNth x (fun m => φ (i.succAbove m))) *
          minkowskiMatrix x (φ i)

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.toDualMapAtIndex_basis_repr_apply_eq_mul
entries.docstring:
In the standard Lorentz basis, raising or lowering an index multiplies the component with that
index fixed by the corresponding diagonal entry of the Minkowski metric.
entries.snippet:
lemma toDualMapAtIndex_basis_repr_apply_eq_mul {d n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → Color}
    (i : Fin (n + 1)) (t : ℝT(d, c))
    (φ : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor d)
      (Function.update c i ((realLorentzTensor d).τ (c i)))) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (Tensor.toDualMapAtIndex (S := realLorentzTensor d) i t) φ =
      (Tensor.basis c).repr t φ * minkowskiMatrix (φ i) (φ i)

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.unitTensor_repr_apply
entries.docstring:
In the standard contravariant and covariant bases, either real Lorentz unit tensor has
Kronecker-delta components.
entries.snippet:
lemma unitTensor_repr_apply {d : ℕ} (c : Color)
    (φ : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor d) ![(realLorentzTensor d).τ c, c]) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (unitTensor (S := realLorentzTensor d) c) φ =
      if φ 0 = φ 1 then 1 else 0

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.inv_eq_self_of_pointwise_eq
TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.inv_id_eq
TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.inv_cast_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma inv_cast_eq {n m : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c1 : Fin m → C} (e : m = n)
    (h : IsReindexing c c1 (Fin.cast e)) (x : Fin n) :
    h.inv (Fin.cast e) x = Fin.cast e.symm x

entries.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.IsReindexing.inv_equiv_symm_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma inv_equiv_symm_eq {n : ℕ} {c c1 : Fin n → C} (e : Equiv.Perm (Fin n))
    (h : IsReindexing c c1 ⇑e.symm) (x : Fin n) :
    h.inv ⇑e.symm x = e x

entries.name: TensorSpecies.unitTensor_basis_repr
entries.docstring:
A component of the unit tensor is the corresponding component of the unit intertwiner in the
tensor-product basis.
entries.snippet:
lemma unitTensor_basis_repr (c : C) (φ : ComponentIdx (S := S) ![S.τ c, c]) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (unitTensor (S := S) c) φ =
      (Module.Basis.tensorProduct (b (S.τ c)) (b c)).repr ((S.unit c) (1 : k))
        (φ 0, φ 1)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame
entries.docstring: A time-indexed choice of affine origin and displacement basis in `d`-dimensional space.
entries.snippet:
structure ReferenceFrame (d : ℕ) where
  origin : Time → Space d
  basis : Time → Module.Basis (Fin d) ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.fromReferencePoints
entries.docstring:
Build a reference frame from the trajectories of a collection of reference points.

At each time, the reference points must form an affine basis: none is redundant, and together they
span the whole space. One reference point is chosen as the origin, and the displacements from it to
the remaining points form the coordinate basis. The resulting frame need not be inertial or
orthonormal.
entries.snippet:
def ReferenceFrame.fromReferencePoints
    (referencePoints : Finset (Time → Space d))
    (independence : ∀ t, AffineIndependent ℝ fun point : referencePoints => point.val t)
    (spans_space : ∀ t, affineSpan ℝ {point.val t | point : referencePoints} = ⊤) :
    ReferenceFrame d

entries.snippet: def IsMetricConserved (frame : ReferenceFrame d) : Prop

structure IsInertial (frame : ReferenceFrame d) : Prop where
  origin_moves_uniformly :
    ∃ velocity, ∀ t₁ t₂, frame.origin t₂ -ᵥ frame.origin t₁ = (t₂ - t₁).val • velocity
  basis_conserved : ∀ t₁ t₂, frame.basis t₁ = frame.basis t₂

entries.name: Space.curl_eq_sum_leviCivitaSymbol
entries.docstring:
The components of the curl as a contraction with the Levi-Civita symbol,
`(∇ ⨯ f) x i = ∑ j k, ε_{ijk} ∂[j] fₖ x`.
entries.snippet:
lemma curl_eq_sum_leviCivitaSymbol (f : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))
    (x : Space) (i : Fin 3) :
    (∇ ⨯ f) x i = ∑ j, ∑ k, (leviCivitaSymbol ![i, j, k] : ℝ) * ∂[j] (fun y => f y k) x

entries.docstring: The canonical equivalence `toRealCLE.symm : ℝ ≃L[ℝ] Time` sends `1 : ℝ` to `1 : Time`.
entries.snippet: lemma toRealCLE_symm_one : toRealCLE.symm (1 : ℝ) = (1 : Time)

entries.name: Time.hasDerivAt_comp_toRealCLE_symm
entries.docstring:
Bridge from the time derivative to `HasDerivAt`: if `w : Time → M` is differentiable at
`toRealCLE.symm τ`, then the curve `τ ↦ w (toRealCLE.symm τ)` on `ℝ` has derivative
`∂ₜ w (toRealCLE.symm τ)` at `τ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma hasDerivAt_comp_toRealCLE_symm [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (w : Time → M) (τ : ℝ) (hw : DifferentiableAt ℝ w (toRealCLE.symm τ)) :
    HasDerivAt (fun τ : ℝ => w (toRealCLE.symm τ)) (∂ₜ w (toRealCLE.symm τ)) τ

entries.name: Time.deriv_comp_toRealCLE_of_hasDerivAt
entries.docstring:
The converse of the bridge `hasDerivAt_comp_toRealCLE_symm`: if the curve `γ : ℝ → M` has
derivative `v` at `toRealCLE t`, then the curve `t ↦ γ (toRealCLE t)` on `Time` has time
derivative `v` at `t`.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_comp_toRealCLE_of_hasDerivAt [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (γ : ℝ → M) (t : Time) (v : M) (h : HasDerivAt γ v (toRealCLE t)) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => γ (toRealCLE s)) t = v

entries.name: Time.deriv_comp_neg
entries.docstring:
The chain rule for the time derivative under the reversal of time: the derivative of
`t ↦ f (-t)` at `t` is minus the derivative of `f` at `-t`.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_comp_neg {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (f : Time → M) (t : Time) (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f (-t)) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => f (-s)) t = -∂ₜ f (-t)

entries.name: Time.deriv_deriv_comp_neg
entries.docstring:
The second derivative is unchanged by the reversal of time: for a smooth curve `f`, the second
derivative of `t ↦ f (-t)` at `t` is the second derivative of `f` at `-t`, the two changes of sign
cancelling.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_deriv_comp_neg {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (f : Time → M) (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f) (t : Time) :
    ∂ₜ (∂ₜ (fun s => f (-s))) t = ∂ₜ (∂ₜ f) (-t)

entries.docstring: The choice of units.

@[ext]
structure LTMCTUnitChoices where
  length : LengthUnit
  time : TimeUnit
  mass : MassUnit
  charge : ChargeUnit
  temperature : TemperatureUnit

entries.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale
entries.docstring:
Given two choices of units `u1` and `u2` and a dimension `d`, the
  element of `ℝ≥0` corresponding to the scaling (by definition) of a quantity of dimension `d`
  when changing from units `u1` to `u2`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def dimScale (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) :Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase →* ℝ≥0 where

entries.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma dimScale_apply (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScale u1 u2 d =
      (u1.length / u2.length) ^ (d.length : ℝ) *
      (u1.time / u2.time) ^ (d.time : ℝ) *
      (u1.mass / u2.mass) ^ (d.mass : ℝ) *
      (u1.charge / u2.charge) ^ (d.charge : ℝ) *
      (u1.temperature / u2.temperature) ^ (d.temperature : ℝ)

entries.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_self
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma dimScale_self (u : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScale u u d = 1

entries.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_one
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma dimScale_one (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) :
    dimScale u1 u2 1 = 1

entries.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_transitive
entries.snippet:
lemma dimScale_transitive (u1 u2 u3 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScale u1 u2 d * dimScale u2 u3 d = dimScale u1 u3 d

entries.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_mul_symm
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma dimScale_mul_symm (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScale u1 u2 d * dimScale u2 u1 d = 1

entries.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_coe_mul_symm
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma dimScale_coe_mul_symm (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    (toReal (dimScale u1 u2 d)) * (toReal (dimScale u2 u1 d)) = 1

entries.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_ne_zero
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma dimScale_ne_zero (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScale u1 u2 d ≠ 0

entries.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_symm
entries.snippet:
lemma dimScale_symm (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScale u1 u2 d = (dimScale u2 u1 d)⁻¹

entries.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_of_inv_eq_swap
entries.snippet:
lemma dimScale_of_inv_eq_swap (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScale u1 u2 d⁻¹ = dimScale u2 u1 d

entries.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.smul_dimScale_injective
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma smul_dimScale_injective {M : Type} [MulAction ℝ≥0 M] (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices)
    (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) (m1 m2 : M) :
    (u1.dimScale u2 d) • m1 = (u1.dimScale u2 d) • m2 ↔ m1 = m2

entries.name: CurrentUnit
entries.docstring:
A unit of electric current — a choice of positive-real magnitude. The SI coherent
  choice is the ampere.
entries.snippet:
structure CurrentUnit where
  val : ℝ
  property : 0 < val

entries.name: CurrentUnit.val_ne_zero
entries.snippet:

entries.name: CurrentUnit.val_pos

entries.name: CurrentUnit.«instance@5ee505c0»
entries.snippet: noncomputable instance : HDiv CurrentUnit CurrentUnit ℝ≥0 where

entries.name: CurrentUnit.div_eq_val
entries.snippet:
lemma div_eq_val (x y : CurrentUnit) :
    x / y = (⟨x.val / y.val, div_nonneg x.val_pos.le y.val_pos.le⟩ : ℝ≥0)

entries.name: CurrentUnit.scale
entries.docstring: Scale a unit of electric current by a positive real factor.
entries.snippet: def scale (r : ℝ) (x : CurrentUnit) (hr : 0 < r := by norm_num) : CurrentUnit

entries.name: CurrentUnit.scale_div_self
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma scale_div_self (x : CurrentUnit) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) :
    scale r x hr / x = (⟨r, le_of_lt hr⟩ : ℝ≥0)

entries.name: CurrentUnit.self_div_scale
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma self_div_scale (x : CurrentUnit) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) :
    x / scale r x hr =
      (⟨1 / r, _root_.div_nonneg (by simp) (le_of_lt hr)⟩ : ℝ≥0)

entries.name: CurrentUnit.scale_one
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma scale_one (x : CurrentUnit) : scale 1 x = x

entries.name: CurrentUnit.scale_div_scale
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma scale_div_scale
    (x1 x2 : CurrentUnit) {r1 r2 : ℝ} (hr1 : 0 < r1) (hr2 : 0 < r2) :
    scale r1 x1 hr1 / scale r2 x2 hr2 =
      (⟨r1, le_of_lt hr1⟩ / ⟨r2, le_of_lt hr2⟩) * (x1 / x2)

entries.name: CurrentUnit.scale_scale
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma scale_scale (x : CurrentUnit) (r1 r2 : ℝ) (hr1 : 0 < r1) (hr2 : 0 < r2) :
    scale r1 (scale r2 x hr2) hr1 =
      scale (r1 * r2) x (mul_pos hr1 hr2)

entries.name: prod_univ_ISQDimensionBase
entries.docstring:
The product over the seven ISQ base quantities, in canonical enumeration order — the
  `ISQDimensionBase` companion to `prod_univ_LTMCTDimensionBase`, a reusable fact about the
  `Fintype` enumeration for folding `Finset.prod` over the ISQ basis.
entries.snippet:
lemma prod_univ_ISQDimensionBase {M : Type} [CommMonoid M] (f : ISQDimensionBase → M) :
    ∏ b, f b = f .length * f .mass * f .time * f .current * f .temperature
      * f .amount * f .luminousIntensity

entries.name: SIUnitChoices
entries.docstring:
A **typed SI unit choice**: a typed unit at every ISQ base quantity. This is the
  seven-slot, current-based sibling of the five-slot, charge-based `LTMCTUnitChoices`,
  produced by the same basis-generic `UnitSystem` / `UnitMagnitudeCatalog` machinery.
entries.snippet: abbrev SIUnitChoices

entries.name: SIUnitChoices.SI
entries.docstring: The coherent SI unit choice: metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, candela.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def SI : SIUnitChoices

entries.name: SIUnitChoices.dimScale
entries.docstring:
The dimension-scaling homomorphism over the ISQ basis, obtained *for free* from the
  generic `UnitScale.dimScale` fold — no per-basis hand-rolling.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def dimScale (u1 u2 : SIUnitChoices) : Dimension ISQDimensionBase →* ℝ≥0

entries.name: SIUnitChoices.dimScale_self
entries.docstring: A quantity of ISQ dimension does not rescale between a unit choice and itself.
entries.snippet:
lemma dimScale_self (u : SIUnitChoices) (d : Dimension ISQDimensionBase) :
    dimScale u u d = 1

entries.name: UnitMagnitudeCatalog
entries.docstring:
A **menu of typed units** for a basis `B`: for each base dimension `b : B`, a *type*
  `Unit b` of admissible units (a dimension may offer several — metre, kilometre, …) and a
  *function* `mag` giving each its single positive-real magnitude. It lists the options and
  picks none — a `UnitSystem` makes the pick. One catalog underlies many unit systems (SI,
  CGS, …); the magnitude is the data `toScale` reads to drive rescaling.
entries.snippet:
class UnitMagnitudeCatalog (B : Type) where
  Unit : B → Type
  mag : {b : B} → Unit b → ℝ≥0
  mag_pos : ∀ {b : B} (u : Unit b), 0 < mag u

entries.name: UnitSystem
entries.docstring:
A **unit system** over a basis `B` with a `UnitMagnitudeCatalog`: one typed unit chosen
  per base dimension — the pick off the catalog's menu, and the formal counterpart of SI,
  CGS, …. Over the default basis, `u .length : LengthUnit`, and a `MassUnit` cannot be
  placed in the length slot.
entries.snippet: def UnitSystem (B : Type) [UnitMagnitudeCatalog B]

entries.name: UnitSystem.ext
entries.docstring:
Two unit systems agree once they pick the same unit at every base dimension: `UnitSystem`
  is extensional, as befits a choice-per-dimension.
entries.snippet:
@[ext]
theorem ext {u v : UnitSystem B} (h : ∀ b, u b = v b) : u = v

entries.name: UnitSystem.toScale
entries.docstring:
Forget a unit system to its magnitude layer `UnitScale B`: keep each chosen unit's
  magnitude, drop its type — the layer where `UnitScale.dimScale` is already proved.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def toScale (u : UnitSystem B) : UnitScale B where

entries.name: UnitSystem.toScale_scale
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toScale_scale (u : UnitSystem B) (b : B) :
    (toScale u).scale b = UnitMagnitudeCatalog.mag (u b)

entries.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.toScale_equivUnitSystem
entries.docstring:
The typed generic projection agrees with the bespoke `LTMCTUnitChoices.toScale`: reading

  the bespoke `toScale`.

entries.name: prod_univ_LTMCTDimensionBase
entries.docstring:
The product over the five default base quantities, in canonical enumeration order — a
  reusable fact about the `Fintype` enumeration of `LTMCTDimensionBase`, for folding
  `Finset.prod` over the default basis (e.g. in a hand-rolled scaling law).
entries.snippet:
lemma prod_univ_LTMCTDimensionBase {M : Type} [CommMonoid M]
    (f : LTMCTDimensionBase → M) :
    ∏ b, f b = f .length * f .time * f .mass * f .charge * f .temperature

LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_eq_toScale_dimScale
entries.docstring:
The hand-rolled five-factor `LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale` equals the basis-generic
  `UnitScale.dimScale` fold at `LTMCTDimensionBase`, applied to `toScale`. The scaling law
  therefore has a single source of truth on the magnitude layer `UnitScale B`.

    u1.dimScale u2 d = UnitScale.dimScale u1.toScale u2.toScale d
